title: Japanese government hires leading comedy agency to explain national defense spending
summary: The number one rule of comedy is unwavering loyalty to the government. I suppose in terms of things on a global scale, the Japanese government isn’t doing all that bad. It’s just that with all the talk of how Prime Minister Takaichi works constantly and rarely sleeps, I was sort of expecting something more in […]
details: The number one rule of comedy is unwavering loyalty to the government . I suppose in terms of things on a global scale, the Japanese government isn’t doing all that bad. It’s just that with all the talk of how Prime Minister Takaichi works constantly and rarely sleeps, I was sort of expecting something more in the way of results. Don’t get me wrong, since coming into power, her cabinet pissed off China right quick, jacked up visa fees , and made it so people can’t poop on the flag . These are all indeed things that were done, and yet, all those efforts don’t seem to have changed the fact that the cost of living in Japan keeps going up and that entire cities are on the verge of being taken over by bears and monkeys . One other thing the Takaichi cabinet has been hard at work at is amending the constitution of Japan to give the military more freedom to take action in overseas conflicts that may not directly threaten the safety of this country. Opponents of this idea say that it goes against the principles of Japan’s previously pacifist constitution, but maybe this is just a very complex situation in an increasingly destabilized world, which may have aspects not everyone is aware of. If only there was a sassy comedy duo that could explain it all in terms an average Joe can understand! And just like that, our prayers are answered. The Government Public Relations Office has teamed up with Japan’s leading comedy talent agency Yoshimoto Kogyo to produce a campaign that explains why some of the seemingly uninspiring things the government’s been doing are actually very good. Yoshimoto specializes in the style of comedy known as manzai . This is a bit of a throwback to the vaudeville era of Western comedy, often involving duos wherein one is the straight man ( tsukkomi ) and the other the funny man ( boke ). This particular series seems to employ a Burns and Allen style combo featuring the husband Kunio and wife Tamiyo, as they trade quips over national policy. ▼ A video trailer for the campaign The art of manzai is largely associated with the culture of Osaka, and is often best delivered in an Osaka dialect and accent, which I prefer to liken to a Staten Island accent, more or less based on vibes alone. There are currently seven pages where Kunio and Tamiyo crack wise about national policy in this manner of speaking, so let’s take a look at their talk about national defense. Tamiyo: “Did you know that Japan’s support ships help sustain our daily lives? They support the world, and Japan is supported as well.” Kunio: “Actually, more than 80 percent of the ships they protect belong to other countries! Japan helps to safeguard its allies, so the world protects Japan in return. We work together and look out for one another, ya know?” … Oh, that’s it? Hahahaha! Granted, it’s hard to make cooperative maritime defense funny, or at least, it’s hard when your job is being a government mouthpiece. Let’s see how they handle some softball topics like the space program instead. Tamiyo: “You ever take it for granted that we can go places we’ve never been before and don’t get lost?” Kunio: “Actually, we’re being guided from space. Japan’s Michibiki satellite system provides us with directions around the clock.” … Sorry, I was thinking about something else there. That one was quite a whiff too, wasn’t it? Alright, let’s take a look at their hot take on AI. This should be a slam dunk since the characters appear to have been hastily generated by AI themselves. Tamiyo: “You think since AI can help with things like planning meals or finding information, it can also be useful for national security?” Kunio: “Actually, efforts are underway to leverage AI so that it can help safeguard the nation.” … Jeez, they’re hardly even using an Osaka dialect in these. Getting a comedy routine down solid is hard work and takes time. We can at least see the seeds of the mansplaining premise beginning to sprout. It all makes me wonder if maybe I’m being too hard on the comedic stylings of Tamiyo and Kunio. Let’s see what online comments say about them. “Are they trying to brainwash us with propaganda now?” “The all-knowing man teaching his dimwitted wife. This really encapsulates why Japan ranks 114th out of 145 countries in the Global Gender Gap Index.” “This is the lowest form of propaganda. I’m done supporting Yoshimoto and won’t buy anything their performers do commercials for.” “They clearly think the public is stupid. They’re looking down on all of us.” “They must think we’re insanely gullible.” “It seems that the country is the role of the ‘husband,’ and the people are the ‘wife,’ which is also just creepy.” “There is no way this will foster understanding. Stop it immediately.” “Don’t waste our tax money on this garbage. If the Prime Minister would just show up in the Diet to provide proper answers or hold actual press conferences, this wouldn’t be necessary!” “This is very dystopian.” I scrolled far and wide and could not find anyone with an even remotely positive thing to say about this campaign. It does not bode well for the government, whose recent lifting of a ban on exporting lethal weapons is currently opposed by about 57 percent of the population, according to a poll by Japan’s Kyodo news organization . Kyodo also cites sources inside the government as saying that explanations of policy that avoid words like “lethal” would be more effective in swaying public opinion. That does sound a tad Orwellian, but we shouldn’t knock it till we try it, so let’s see what Tamiyo and Kunio have to say about the nation’s defense policy. Tamiyo: “You ever think we take uneventful days for granted?” Kunio: “Actually, the fact that nothing newsworthy happened today just goes to show ya. A day where ‘nothing happens’ ain’t no coincidence. It’s the result of tireless work to keep us safe.” Ha! Those two kill me. title: Starbucks Japan unveils new winter drinkware collection with limited-edition Stanley cups
summary: New collection brings warmth and style to tumblers and mugs this winter. When the seasons change in Japan, so too do the limited-edition goods at Starbucks, and this season we’ll be getting a new limited-edition collection just for winter. With icy hues of white and mint green, these items are said to blend easily into […]
details: New collection brings warmth and style to tumblers and mugs this winter. When the seasons change in Japan, so too do the limited-edition goods at Starbucks , and this season we’ll be getting a new limited-edition collection just for winter . With icy hues of white and mint green , these items are said to blend easily into any scenario to “softly illuminate your winter days”, and there are six specially designed products to choose from. ▼ Pale White Stanley Stainless Steel Bottle , 473 millilitres (16 ounces) – 6,350 yen (US$40.11) This leak-proof stainless steel bottle has a sleek and simple design, with a handle built into the lid for easy carrying. The body has a pale white colour that shimmers delicately in the light, adding an air of sophistication to your everyday drinking experience. This is one of the four items in the series that’s also eligible for Starbucks’ online store name engraving service, which lets you add your name and/or a pictogram to the back, bringing the total to 7,450 yen. ▼ Mint Green Stainless Steel To Go Tumbler – 473 millilitres (4,600 yen) The body of this stainless steel tumbler has a soothing mint green hue, while the shape is inspired by Starbucks’ paper cups, making it suitable for a wide range of scenarios, from everyday use to office settings. This product is also eligible for the online store’s personalisation service, which raises the price to 5,700 yen. ▼ Mint Green Logo Cold Cup Tumbler – 710 millilitres (3,050 yen) This tumbler features an eye-catching, diamond-cut design that gives off a different look depending on how the light hits it. The straw, which allows you to easily enjoy cold drinks, also has a textured surface that catches the light, adding a touch of elegance to your drink time. ▼ White Stainless Steel Cold Cup Tumbler – 591 millilitres (5,350 yen) This user-friendly tumbler features an easy-to-grip handle and a removable straw, for use with cold beverages only. With the personalisation service, the total price of the tumbler comes to 6,450 yen. ▼ Mint Green Stainless Steel Mug – 355 millilitres (3,800 yen) The mint green hues on this stainless steel mug add a sense of calmness to the simple design while the debossed Siren logo creates a subtle accent. The lid features a drinking spout and a slide-open mechanism for ease of use, and if you opt for the personalisation service the total comes to 4,900 yen. ▼ Mint Green Heat-resistant Glass Mug – 296 millilitres (3,500 yen) This glass mug features a unique base filled with glittery confetti that swirls about as you enjoy your drink. The transparent design allows you to enjoy the color of your drink alongside the elegant, sparkly confetti. The new collection is a beautiful way to add a sense of warmth and luxury to wintry drinks, and they can be purchased at Starbucks stores and online while stocks last. title: Giant Code Geass C.C. plush stands over three feet tall and costs $420
summary: C.C. from Code Geass is getting a plushie that turns the green-haired anime girl into a giant three-foot-tall collectible.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 Entertainment Giant Code Geass C.C. plush stands over three feet tall and costs $420 by James Busby Published: Nov 05, 2026, 11:03 Save for later Save for later TAITO GEAR&GOODS Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News C.C. from the popular anime Code Geass is getting a plushie that turns the green-haired girl into a giant three-foot-tall collectible. It’s been a big year for monolithic anime merch, with everything from a life-size Marin Kitagawa figure with an $8,000 price tag to giant Snorlax body pillows . However, fans of the popular mecha anime Code Geass will soon be able to celebrate the show’s 20th anniversary in style with a plushie so big that it needs its own dedicated spot on your sofa. title: Dragon Ball Daima censored in France to erase Mr Popo, but fans can still hear him
summary: Dragon Ball Daima has completely removed Mr. Popo in France, with the character being edited out of scenes despite his voice remaining.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 TV & Movies Anime Dragon Ball Daima censored in France to erase Mr Popo, but fans can still hear him by Michael Gwilliam Published: Nov 05, 2026, 20:40 Save for later Save for later Crunchyroll Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News Dragon Ball Daima has completely removed Mr. Popo from the screen in France, with the character being edited out of scenes despite his voice remaining in the anime. The latest installment in Akira Toriyama’s iconic franchise originally debuted in October 2024 , following Goku and his allies as they’re transformed into children and forced to venture into the Demon Realm. On November 4, 2026, Daima made its French television debut on Gulli, but viewers quickly noticed that one familiar character was nowhere to be seen. Article continues after ad As reported by Journal du Geek , Mr. Popo, the longtime attendant of Kami and later Dende, had been completely erased from the screen. Rather than simply cutting his dialogue, scenes featuring the character were removed, cropped, or edited to ensure he never appeared on camera. Strangely enough, however, his voice can still be heard in certain scenes, meaning the character technically still exists in the French version. Article continues after ad Mr Popo a été supprimé de Dragon Ball Daima en France ! Il parle, mais n'apparait pas à l'image !! LA HONTE 😑 @ToeiAnimationEU … Non mais sérieux…. pic.twitter.com/h1z5nxseaL — Tony Graci (@Tony_Mr_P) November 4, 2026 “Mr. Popo has been removed from Dragon Ball Daima in France! He speaks, but doesn’t appear on screen!” one furious fan wrote on X. Article continues after ad Another report indicated that Episode 2 received similar treatment, with scenes heavily re-edited and zoomed in to hide Mr. Popo. Why was Mr Popo censored in Dragon Ball Daima? The character’s design has been controversial for decades, with critics arguing that his dark skin, exaggerated red lips, and other features resemble racist caricatures. EN FRANCE, LE PERSONNAGE DE MR POPO DANS L’ANIME DRAGON BALL : DAIMA A ÉTÉ CENSURÉ ! ❌ La voix du personnage est présente dans les épisodes, mais il n’apparaît pas à l’écran. pic.twitter.com/bHBkeZXHex — INKU (@Inku_fr) November 4, 2026 However, defenders of the design argue that Mr. Popo was never intended to represent a black person. Fans have pointed to similarities with Mahakala , a dark-skinned guardian deity in Buddhist and Hindu traditions, suggesting his appearance draws from religious imagery rather than racist stereotypes. Related Dragon Ball Daima release date, trailer, & everything else you should know Dragon Ball Daima episode one anime details leak ahead of 2024 release Dragon Ball Daima divides fans with new character designs Article continues after ad This isn’t even the first time Dragon Ball has censored him. In the American CW broadcast of Dragon Ball Z Kai in 2010, Mr. Popo was famously recolored blue. France also isn’t the first country to remove him from Daima. Germany’s broadcast received similar edits when the anime premiered on Toggo Plus in August 2026. Article continues after ad It’s currently unclear whether the French censorship was ordered by Gulli or Toei Animation Europe, and neither has publicly confirmed the reason behind the changes. Article continues after ad The controversy is particularly notable given Toriyama’s involvement in Daima’s story and character designs , with the anime even offering new clues about Mr. Popo’s mysterious origins. For fans wanting to see the original version, all 20 episodes of Dragon Ball Daima are available uncensored with subtitles on streaming services including Crunchyroll and Netflix in France. title: Pachinko parlor operator arrested for not obscuring the act of gambling well enough
summary: If you’re going to do wrong, do wrong right. For many years, pachinko parlors have stood tall and proud in just about every community across the country as bastions of the human desire to make quick money without having to work for it. Every day, thousands and thousands of people flock to the large and […]
details: If you’re going to do wrong, do wrong right . For many years, pachinko parlors have stood tall and proud in just about every community across the country as bastions of the human desire to make quick money without having to work for it. Every day, thousands and thousands of people flock to the large and comfortably equipped complexes, seemingly never realizing that the main reason these places are so large and comfortably equipped is that they’re the ones ending up with the money. It should be noted that pachinko is technically not gambling, however. Japan has frowned on the vice of gambling for most of its history, with the exception of government-run operations of horse racing, boat racing, bicycle racing, and the lottery, as well as a recently enacted law allowing strictly managed casinos in integrated resorts. ▼ You get four forms of gambling and that’s it! OK, fine! Five, but that’s really it! Even when pachinko players win, they get no money awarded by the parlor . Depending on the performance of the player, they are awarded metal balls by the machine. They’re kind of like the tickets you’d get from a skee-ball machine, and in the same way, you can trade in the balls at a counter in the parlor for wonderful “special prizes” ( tokushu keihin ) . These prizes can be ordinary arbitrary items like pens or lighter flint, but many places nowadays award cards with tiny pieces of gold in them to help prevent counterfeiting. ▼ It takes a lot of balls to play this game. As luck would have it, right beside, or at least not too far from the pachinko parlor, there is always a store owned by people who seem to really love these special prizes. If you go here, you can sell them for ridiculously more than they’re actually worth and walk away with a nice chunk of change from a legitimate sale of your newfound special prizes . It’s a bit of a silly business model if you ask me, which must be why these places are often very modest-looking and have little to no signage. ▼ On your right is a pachinko parlor and on the left is a shop that buys prizes for a pachinko parlor. It may look like the same business, but that store is technically in a different building and owned by a different company, and what’s with all the questions anyway? What, are you a cop or something? Of course, since they offer such amazing prices for these prizes, they often end up with too many. But a lucky coincidence strikes again in the form of a wholesaler who is willing to buy those items from the shop, practically at cost, and sell them back to the pachinko parlors, once again, practically at cost . Since these are all legit sales, the government gets its piece of the action in the form of taxes, and everyone’s happy… except those players without wonderful special prizes, of whom there are many. This circle of life is called the “ santen hoshiki ” or “three-store system,” and it’s what separates dirty, yucky gambling from shiny, happy free-market capitalism. But should a pachinko parlor take it upon themselves to not follow the three-store system, trouble awaits, as it did recently in Miyagi Prefecture. On October 30th, it was reported that charges were filed against the manager and operating company of a pachinko parlor in the city of Ishinomaki. According to the charges, on 20 January, the parlor purchased four special prizes from a customer for a total of 3,500 yen (US$22), thus bypassing the three-store system and awarding cash prizes for games of chance. This parlor had since closed down, but the 71-year-old manager confessed to the act. This is the first such case to occur in Miyazaki since 2007. Readers of the news expressed understandable confusion in comments with regard to what the heck is actually going on with pachinko in Japan in the first place. “Seriously, why is the three-store system only permitted for pachinko parlors? Has that ever actually been explained?” “Why go through with all this superficial nonsense? Just ban pachinko for crying out loud.” “This is kind of absurd, isn’t it?” “In Asakusa [in Tokyo] there’s an exchange booth for a pachinko parlor right next to a police box.” “There’s probably some other crime involved they want to look into.” “Funny how pachinko parlor staff never seem to notice the mysterious little shacks sitting right on their own premises.” “The three-shop system is inherently illegal, isn’t it?” “I’ll just go and set up my own three-shop system then.” While it sounds like a great idea to set up your own casino and only give away prizes that can be cycled through the three-store system, that will likely land you in prison. As mentioned in the comments, this system is only applicable to pachinko and slot machines. All other games are regulated differently . Casino games are the most highly regulated, and if the house gives out so much as a mustache comb, they’ll get shut down faster than you can say, “A mustache comb? What the f…” Arcades, or “game centers” as they’re called in Japan, also have regulations on awarding prizes of any kind. One exception are UFO catchers, and this is mainly because in these games, the entire point is to grab the item. However, they are strictly regulated as well, and the prizes they offer cannot exceed a wholesale price of 1,000 yen per item. ▼ That’s a good fact to know when considering a lucky bag claw game . Another interesting example of pseudo-gambling in Japan are those high-end gacha machines where you pay 1,000 yen for a chance to get a Gucci bag or PS5 . The reason these aren’t gambling is because they aren’t even classified as games. They’re technically vending machines from which straight purchases are made, and they will be treated as such as long as the customer never “loses” in the sense of getting an empty capsule or booby prize. Long-time readers of our site might remember our writer Masanuki Sunakoma getting an endless array of junk from those machines, like gearbox keychains and talon necklaces. title: Pokémon doughnuts pop up at Mister Donut, with a new gathering that’s bigger than ever
summary: The “Everyone Gather Together! Winter Pokémon Campaign” goes all out for the 30th anniversary celebrations. It’s become something of an annual tradition for Mister Donut to release a new Pokémon collection at the end of the year, with a different pocket monster taking centre stage as the star of the show. This year, however, for […]
details: The “Everyone Gather Together! Winter Pokémon Campaign” goes all out for the 30th anniversary celebrations. It’s become something of an annual tradition for Mister Donut to release a new Pokémon collection at the end of the year, with a different pocket monster taking centre stage as the star of the show. This year, however, for Pokémon’s 30th anniversary , the chain is going all out with the celebrations, putting not just one Pokémon in the spotlight, but a whole gathering from past campaigns. ▼ The promo image reads “Atsumare! Minna!” (“Gather! Everyone!”) Image: Press release With this being the ninth Pokémon x Mister Donut collaboration collection, there are a lot of characters returning for the celebrations, and Mister Donut says every Pokémon that has appeared in previous collaborations will be coming together for this year’s collection. Leading the charge on the doughnut front is Alolan Diglett , who differs from the Diglett that appeared previously with a different coating and a gummy nose instead of a chocolate one. ▼ Oh, and a chocolate rendering of its head tuft, seeing as it’s Alolan. The theme for this year’s collaboration is “ Alolan Diglett Brings Everyone Together! ” and while the doughnuts are limited to Alolan Diglett and fan favourite Pikachu , the Pokémon gathering takes place on the limited-edition merchandise that can be bought as a set with the doughnuts. There’s also a cream-filled choux doughnut called “ Pokémon Friends Gather! Angel & Custard “, which comes in one of four randomly selected sleeves featuring the Pokémon characters. The “Goods Set” (2,200 yen for takeout, 2,217 yen for dine-in) gets you two Pokémon doughnuts of your choice, one doughnut from a choice of two “Pon de Wreath” varieties, a choice of one of two blankets, and an original paper bag. The “Kids Goods Set” gets you one Pokémon doughnut, one doughnut from the choice of two “Pon de Wreath” varieties, a limited-edition Pokémon glass and an original paper bag. ▼ We stopped by to get our hands on the “Goods Set”, which came in this gorgeous bag. When we returned home, we laid out our haul, and couldn’t help but admire the cute characters that sat in front of use, including on the doughnut box. Taking a closer look at the blanket, there are two to choose from, blue and orange, and we went for the orange one, which features plenty of Grass-type Pokémon and other warm-coloured characters. Each blanket has a different selection of Pokémon, so you can either choose the one that has your favourite characters, or purchase two sets to catch ’em all. The blankets look much the same as they do every year, but this time they seem to have been made slightly bigger. They’ve increased in height, making them closer to square than the horizontally elongated rectangles of previous years, giving you more coverage for use as a lap blanket, which is a welcome improvement. It is rather thin, though, and amounts to around 1,200 yen of the price of the set so it’s not entirely a bargain, but it is an exclusive you won’t find anywhere else so it’s still a sought-after item for fans. ▼ Last year’s blanket on top, compared to this year’s slightly larger version below. As for the doughnuts, they looked as cute as ever, and Alolan Diglett was particularly delicious, thanks to its chocolate-coated doughnut base and whipped-cream-filled centre. This year, Pikachu appears in its fluffy form for the second year running, and is still filled with the same whipped cream, with custard-flavoured flakes sprinkled across its surface. ▼ Like last year, Pikachu has rosy pink cheeks, even though they really ought to be red, if we’re going to be true to the character. Both doughnuts were as cute as they were delicious, but the party doesn’t end there, as Mister Donut says it will be bringing out a Slowpoke doughnut to join the collection from 25 November. ▼ Online reservations for the new doughnut begin on 18 November. Image: Press release The current Pokémon collection went on sale across Japan from 4 November, but only in limited stocks so you’ll want to head out early to find them or reserve them through Mister Donut’s online ordering service to ensure you don’t miss out. title: Discount retailers known for massive bargains releases massive Japanese egg sandwich
summary: Don Quijote doubles up its “Peculiar Preference” sandwich. Japanese egg sandwiches have recently become an unexpected hit among the international foodie community, but within Japan, they’ve been a staple for generations. You really don’t have to go very far to find one, as just about every convenience store or supermarket stocks them. But if you […]
details: Don Quijote doubles up its “Peculiar Preference” sandwich . Japanese egg sandwiches have recently become an unexpected hit among the international foodie community, but within Japan, they’ve been a staple for generations. You really don’t have to go very far to find one, as just about every convenience store or supermarket stocks them. But if you really love Japan’s egg sandwiches, it’s worth going to the little extra trouble of making a trip to discount retailer Don Quixote to get one, because not only are they massive, right now they’re even bigger than they usually are. Among tourists, Don Quijote is most famous for their selection of quirky souvenirs and affordable cosmetics, but they also sell clothing, toiletries, housewares, and, at some locations, even food items, including ready to eat bento boxed lunches and sandwiches. With the chain being popular with a broad range of shoppers, you’d expect them to want to offer foodstuffs that anyone would like. However, for their Henai Meshi , or “Peculiar Preference Food,” line, Don Quijote isn’t worried about fully satisfying everybody. In fact, the goal of Henai Meshi is to create meals “that most people would give 75 points out of 100, but that some people will give 120,” like the Bento with Fried Chicken Skin Only that they offered a while back. The Henai Meshi egg sandwich isn’t so unusual in terms of it ingredients, but their quantity could be considered egregious by some, as each sandwich is made with two and a half soft-boiled eggs. Right now, though, Don Quijote is running a special promotion in which it’s increasing the size of selected Henai Meshi items, and one of those is the egg sandwich, which has doubled in size and now contains five eggs! The Five Melty Soft-boiled Egg Sandwich is priced at 430 yen (US$2.70), and if you’re thinking it’s got to be hefty to hold, you’re exactly right. We were curious as to just how heavy it was, so once we got back to the SoraNews24 taste-testing center, before digging in we placed it on a scale… …which gave us a weight of 418 grams (roughly 14.75 ounces) . Granted, a small fraction of that is the plastic packaging, but still, this is close to a pound of eggs and bread . There’s so much egg that the strips of bread between them start to look like garnish, or maybe just something to keep your fingers clean as you eat a whole tray of eggs. Taste-testing was handled by our Japanese-language reporter P.K. Sanjun, who informs us that, in his estimation, the Five Melty Soft-boiled Egg Sandwich completely misses the mark for the Henai Meshi series. However, that’s not a complaint, because he clarifies that instead of being something that most people would give 75 point to and some would give 120, this sandwich is so delicious that he thinks most people would give it 95 out of a 100 . Of course, while we’re talking about numerical measurements, your dietician probably wouldn’t be too thrilled about what eating five eggs at once would do to your cholesterol levels. However, with Don Quiojote’s double-sized egg sandwich only being available from November 1 to 10 , there’s not time really enough time to do all that much dietary damage, making this a decadent special-occasion indulgence P.K. is very happy to have treated himself to. title: Tokyo to build new crematoriums to meet surging demand
summary: Death is a growth industry that no one’s happy about. There has been a lot of talk about the aging population in Japan and how it’s affecting society and the economy. But a more immediate concern is how to handle the influx of people currently dying across the country. According to estimates, the number of […]
details: Death is a growth industry that no one’s happy about . There has been a lot of talk about the aging population in Japan and how it’s affecting society and the economy. But a more immediate concern is how to handle the influx of people currently dying across the country. According to estimates, the number of deaths per year is expected to swell to a peak of 1.65 million in 2040, but with the current number over 1.5 million, Japan looks poised to overshoot that estimate considerably . Large cities in particular are starting to feel the strain, since the common method of internment in Japan is cremation. Luckily, this means cemetery space can be kept rather small, but the facilities to perform cremations are limited. There have been reports of crematoriums in Chiba Prefecture issuing wait times of as many as 10 days, and supply and demand has also seen the costs of such services rise as well. In normal businesses, this would attract other competitors who would eventually bring down prices, but that is especially difficult for crematoriums as they are very costly to set up and zoning laws make it very hard to even find a place to put a facility for burning human remains. ▼ Urayasu Crematorium is located right beside Tokyo Disneyland, you can see just a bit of it if you look to your left along with the Tokyo Skytree in the distance. Nowhere is this situation more severe then the dense metropolis of Tokyo, whose government recently decided to take matters into their own hands and are drafting a proposal to build a series of small-scale publicly run crematoriums throughout the 23 wards . They will focus on adding locations where they are needed most, and if necessary, relax zoning laws to allow them to fit. That’s not to say the private sector is sitting around doing nothing. In recent years, Japan has seen the emergence of what is colloquially called “itai hotels” (literally “corpse hotels”) . These are facilities that refrigerate the body so it is preserved until cremation can be made available, while also allowing loved ones to visit in a respectful, home-like environment. True to the name, they even offer rates comparable to a hotel’s, ranging from 10,000 to 200,000 per day depending on size and quality. ▼ News report showing the inside of an itai hotel The real difficulty in these projects is that, despite how serious the problem is now, it’s destined to be a temporary one because of Japan’s shrinking population , making it harder to make a case for large-scale infrastructure investment. At least if governments take the initiative in building new crematoriums, they can be shut down more easily when no longer needed, and itai hotels are more or less standard commercial facilities that can be easily repurposed. It’s an awkward situation that Japan is still trying to feel its way around, but it’s something many other countries are going to have to face in the coming years. Hopefully, others can learn from what goes right and what goes wrong here. title: Continuing cyberattacks hit Japanese arcade hard [Photos]
summary: Preserving arcade culture is hard enough without hacker jerks making it even tougher. A photo of an empty interior and unused game machines accompanied by the message “This is the harsh reality for arcades right now” might be the kind of thing that would make gamers sad, but not necessarily surprised. Though the video game […]
details: Preserving arcade culture is hard enough without hacker jerks making it even tougher . A photo of an empty interior and unused game machines accompanied by the message “This is the harsh reality for arcades right now” might be the kind of thing that would make gamers sad, but not necessarily surprised. Though the video game business as a whole is bigger than ever, the ways that people play them has changed significantly since the arcade glory days of the ‘80s and ‘90s, and the industry trend in Japan has become one of arcades steadily reducing the amount of floorspace they devote to video games while installing more and more UFO catcher/crane/claw prize machines. But a recent tweet from the Machida branch of arcade chain Taito Station in Tokyo doesn’t show just row after row of unoccupied games, but ones with dark screens too . ゲームセンターの過酷な現状… お客様の皆様には大変御迷惑お掛けしています。 pic.twitter.com/gF1YjwSEZ9 — タイステ町田 (@Taito_Machida) November 5, 2026 The reason for all that dark emptiness isn’t because the arcade’s entire customer base decided they’d rather be somewhere else playing Fortnite on their phones. No, it’s because, as with so many other things these days, of the huge increase in hacks, cyberattacks, and other online maliciousness and jackassery over the past few weeks. One of the ways the surviving arcade video game franchises have survived is by embracing online/network play, especially if it’s coupled to some sort of deluxe control or display hardware that would be impractically large or expensive for many people’s homes, such as a full steering wheel and pedals, expansive dance step sensors, card readers, or gigantic touchscreen arrays. Combine that feeling of immersion with the ability to race, fight, or otherwise compete with other players, either in real-time or through leaderboards, and you can cultivate a customer community by connecting modestly sized, geographically separated pockets of fans. Unfortunately, that means that if a game network’s security is compromised and it has to be shut down, either in response to a hack or as a preventive measure, the game has to be shut down too . Network play is so integrated into many Japanese arcade games that the first thing they do upon booting up is try to connect to their network, and some can’t progress to a playable state until they can successfully do so, resulting in situations like the one shown in the Taito Station Machida tweet, in which the arcade says “We deeply apologize for the great inconvenience to our customers.” 一角は営業中かも危ぶまれるような写真ですがちゃんと稼働しているゲームも勿論有りますので是非ともご利用下さいね！ #タイステ #町田 pic.twitter.com/bcDo1HmieB — タイステ町田 (@Taito_Machida) November 5, 2026 Thankfully, not every game in the arcade has had to go offline, and classic titles that don’t require a network connection are unaffected , so, as shown in the above follow-up tweet, Taito Station Matsuda still has games that can be played, and they invite gamers to come in for them. Other arcades are likely dealing with similar problems, so if you’re a gamer with a few spare 100-yen coins in your wallet, they’d probably appreciate a visit, even if your regular favorites aren’t currently playable. title: Fool Night revela tráiler: en este mundo te pagan por convertirte en planta
summary: Fool Night revela un nuevo tráiler, elenco y temas musicales. El oscuro anime de Sunrise y SHAFT llegará a Netflix el 26 de noviembre de 2026.
details: Anime Fool Night revela tráiler: en este mundo te pagan por convertirte en planta Sunrise y SHAFT estrenarán esta oscura historia de ciencia ficción en Netflix el próximo 26 de noviembre. Kudasai hace 2 horas 1 Comentarios ADS ¿Hasta dónde estarías dispuesto a llegar para conseguir dinero? Probablemente convertirte en una planta no estaría entre tus primeras opciones, pero en el mundo de Fool Night las cosas funcionan de manera bastante diferente. Bandai Namco Filmworks presentó un nuevo tráiler y una imagen promocional de esta adaptación al anime del manga de Kasumi Yasuda, confirmando también nuevas voces y los artistas encargados de sus temas musicales. La serie llegará a Netflix el 26 de noviembre de 2026 , con todos sus episodios disponibles desde el primer día. El avance permite conocer mejor la extraña sociedad donde se desarrolla la historia, además de mostrar algunas escenas bastante inquietantes relacionadas con la transformación de humanos en plantas. Por otra parte, se confirmó que Tempalay interpretará el opening titulado Shake! spit out , mientras que Nowlu estará a cargo del ending Iki . Y por si la premisa no fuera suficientemente llamativa, tendremos a Sunrise y SHAFT trabajando juntos por primera vez en una misma producción. Un mundo donde convertirse en planta puede salvarte de la pobreza La historia de Fool Night se desarrolla en un futuro donde enormes nubes han bloqueado la luz del sol durante aproximadamente cien años. Como consecuencia, la vegetación prácticamente ha desaparecido y la humanidad enfrenta una grave escasez de oxígeno. Para sobrevivir, los científicos desarrollaron la transfloración , un procedimiento que permite convertir a personas cercanas a la muerte en plantas capaces de producir oxígeno. El problema es que esta tecnología también terminó convirtiéndose en una salida desesperada para quienes no tienen suficiente dinero. Entre ellos se encuentra Toshiro Kamiya, un joven que apenas consigue sobrevivir con su miserable salario mientras intenta pagar los medicamentos de su madre enferma. Sin demasiadas alternativas, comienza a considerar vender su propio cuerpo para someterse a la transfloración y recibir una compensación económica. Sin embargo, las cosas toman un rumbo inesperado cuando Toshiro descubre que puede escuchar las voces de las personas que ya fueron transformadas en plantas. Esta peculiar habilidad terminará involucrándolo en una investigación relacionada con una serie de asesinatos, donde los responsables parecen estar conectados con los secretos de la transfloración. Así que nuestro protagonista no solamente tendrá que preocuparse por conseguir dinero, sino también por descubrir qué está ocurriendo detrás de este sistema. El anime suma voces de Dandadan y My Hero Academia En cuanto al elenco de voces, se anunciaron cinco integrantes adicionales que acompañarán a Koki Uchiyama, quien interpretará al protagonista Toshiro Kamiya. Entre las nuevas incorporaciones destacan: Sumi Matsuno: Shion Wakayama, conocida por interpretar a Momo Ayase en Dandadan . Ken Hikasa: Hiroshi Tsuchida, actor de voz que participó en producciones como Attack on Titan . Nishi: Nobuhiko Okamoto, reconocido por interpretar a Katsuki Bakugo en My Hero Academia . Meg Okumura: Sayaka Senbongi, quien dio voz a Marcille Donato en Delicious in Dungeon . Ivy: Yumiko Kobayashi, conocida por interpretar a Shinnosuke Nohara en Crayon Shin-chan . Un detalle especialmente emotivo es la participación de Hiroshi Tsuchida, quien falleció el pasado 11 de octubre a los 54 años. El actor interpretará a Ken Hikasa, un hombre que se opone al sistema de transfloración, y los responsables del anime compartieron un mensaje que había preparado antes de su fallecimiento. En él, Tsuchida habló sobre las convicciones de su personaje y las preguntas que su historia podría despertar entre los espectadores. Respecto al equipo de producción, Atsushi Yukawa estará a cargo de la dirección , mientras que Jin Tanaka se encargará de la composición de la serie, después de haber trabajado en proyectos como Oshi no Ko . Los diseños de personajes serán responsabilidad de Robert Sato, con Tatsuya Kato encargado de la banda sonora. Cabe recordar que el manga original de Fool Night comenzó a publicarse en noviembre de 2020 dentro de la revista Big Comic Superior de Shogakukan. La obra ya cuenta con trece volúmenes recopilatorios y ha superado el millón de copias en circulación. Su adaptación también marcará la primera colaboración entre Sunrise, conocido por franquicias como Mobile Suit Gundam , y SHAFT, responsable de Puella Magi Madoka Magica y la franquicia Monogatari . ¿Aceptarías convertirte en una planta a cambio de una buena cantidad de dinero, o preferirías seguir siendo humano aunque tuvieras que vivir en la pobreza? title: Spirit Circle tendrá anime después de 10 años y será la despedida del director de Nadesico
summary: Spirit Circle tendrá anime en diciembre de 2026 con 18 episodios. La obra de Satoshi Mizukami será el último trabajo del director Tatsuo Sato.
details: Anime Spirit Circle tendrá anime después de 10 años y será la despedida del director de Nadesico La obra de Satoshi Mizukami se estrenará en diciembre de 2026 con 18 episodios y una historia de reencarnaciones. Ryo hace 2 horas 1 Comentarios ADS Imagínate conocer a una chica en tu escuela y descubrir que lleva varias vidas intentando matarte. Pues esa es apenas una parte de los problemas que tendrá que enfrentar el protagonista de Spirit Circle , el popular manga de Satoshi Mizukami que finalmente dará el salto a la animación. Se anunció oficialmente que la obra tendrá una adaptación al anime de 18 episodios , cuyo estreno está programado para diciembre de 2026. El anuncio llegó acompañado de un primer tráiler, una imagen promocional y los integrantes principales del elenco de voces. La noticia tiene un significado especial para los seguidores del autor, pues el manga terminó su publicación hace una década. Pero también habrá un motivo para recordar esta producción dentro de la industria: será el último trabajo del director Tatsuo Sato , quien falleció en abril de este año y dejó el proyecto en manos de sus colaboradores para que pudiera completarse. La historia sigue a Fuuta Okeya, un estudiante de secundaria que tiene la peculiar habilidad de ver espíritus. Aunque normalmente lleva una vida bastante tranquila, todo cambia cuando conoce a Kouko Ishigami, una misteriosa estudiante recién transferida que parece tener algo personal contra él. Y no estamos hablando de una simple discusión escolar, pues la muchacha asegura que necesita matarlo para romper una maldición que los mantiene conectados desde sus vidas anteriores. El problema es que Fuuta no tiene la menor idea de qué hizo para ganarse semejante enemiga. Para descubrirlo, tendrá que recorrer sus propias reencarnaciones mediante un misterioso círculo espiritual, experimentando diferentes existencias que abarcan desde civilizaciones antiguas hasta un futuro lejano. A medida que recupera los recuerdos de sus otras vidas, comenzará a comprender la verdadera naturaleza de su relación con Kouko y los acontecimientos que terminaron enfrentándolos. La adaptación abordará siete vidas conectadas entre sí , algo que el propio Satoshi Mizukami reconoció como un desafío para el equipo de animación. El mangaka agradeció a los responsables por conseguir trasladar una historia que cambia constantemente de época, personajes y escenarios, especialmente considerando que dispondrán de una duración poco habitual de dieciocho episodios. El último anime de Tatsuo Sato reunirá voces de Blue Lock y Jujutsu Kaisen En cuanto al equipo de producción, Tatsuo Sato estuvo a cargo de la dirección y los guiones , después de haber trabajado en títulos como Martian Successor Nadesico , Stellvia y Bodacious Space Pirates . Lamentablemente, el director falleció en abril de 2026 a los 61 años, por lo que Spirit Circle será su última producción como director. El proyecto fue completado bajo la supervisión del asistente de dirección Kentaro Mizuno, respetando el trabajo y las decisiones creativas que Sato había dejado establecidas. La animación correrá por cuenta de los estudios NAGOMI y EOTA, con TWIN ENGINE encargada de la producción. Por su parte, Satoru Fujimoto será responsable del diseño de personajes. También se confirmaron los cuatro integrantes principales del elenco de voces: Fuuta Okeya: Kazuki Ura, conocido por interpretar a Yoichi Isagi en Blue Lock . Kouko Ishigami: Anna Nagase, quien dio voz a Ushio Kofune en Summer Time Rendering y Riko Amanai en Jujutsu Kaisen . Rune: Eri Yukimura, reconocida por interpretar a Fuyuko Mayuzumi en The Idolmaster Shiny Colors . East: Yuichi Nakamura, la voz de Satoru Gojo en Jujutsu Kaisen . Además, Anna Nagase interpretará el ending titulado Koko ga Donna Sekai Demo (No Matter the World), una canción compuesta especialmente para la serie que también puede escucharse durante el primer avance promocional. La actriz explicó que intentó reflejar tanto los sentimientos dolorosos como el afecto que existe entre los personajes, marcando también su debut con una canción como solista. Cabe recordar que el manga original de Spirit Circle comenzó a publicarse en mayo de 2012 dentro de la revista Young King Ours de Shonengahosha, concluyendo en marzo de 2016 con un total de seis volúmenes recopilatorios . Su autor, Satoshi Mizukami, también es conocido por obras como The Lucifer and Biscuit Hammer y Sengoku Youko , que anteriormente recibieron sus propias adaptaciones animadas. Por ahora, no se ha revelado una fecha exacta de estreno dentro de diciembre, aunque se confirmó que la serie tendrá distribución internacional. Después de diez años desde la conclusión del manga, sus lectores finalmente podrán ver esta historia de reencarnaciones en movimiento. ¿Te llaman la atención las historias donde los protagonistas tienen que resolver problemas de sus vidas pasadas, o crees que siete reencarnaciones son demasiadas para una sola pareja de enemigos? title: Dragon Ball Super: Beerus recupera las voces clásicas: ya hay fecha para el doblaje latino
summary: Dragon Ball Super: Beerus estrenará su doblaje latino en Crunchyroll el 12 de noviembre, con Mario Castañeda, René García y episodios semanales.
details: Anime Dragon Ball Super: Beerus recupera las voces clásicas: ya hay fecha para el doblaje latino Mario Castañeda y René García regresan el 12 de noviembre a Crunchyroll, con nuevos episodios cada semana. Aiko hace 3 horas 3 Comentarios ADS Podrán mejorar la animación de Dragon Ball Super todo lo que quieran, pero hay algo que los fanáticos latinoamericanos seguramente no estarían dispuestos a cambiar: las voces de Goku y Vegeta. Crunchyroll y Toei Animation confirmaron que Dragon Ball Super: Beerus tendrá doblaje latino a partir del próximo 12 de noviembre de 2026, permitiendo que los seguidores de la franquicia disfruten de esta versión mejorada con las interpretaciones que conocen desde hace años. El anuncio llegó acompañado de un tráiler doblado al español, donde podemos escuchar nuevamente a Mario Castañeda como Goku y René García como Vegeta. También regresan José Luis Orozco interpretando a Bills, el Dios de la Destrucción, y Arturo Castañeda como Whis. Por lo visto, no tendremos que acostumbrarnos a nuevas voces para los personajes principales, aunque todavía quedan algunas dudas sobre cómo se ha trabajado el doblaje de esta edición. La plataforma confirmó que los episodios doblados llegarán cada jueves , comenzando el 12 de noviembre a las 10:00 de la mañana, hora de la Ciudad de México. Además del español latino, la producción también estará disponible con doblajes al inglés y portugués, por lo que los seguidores de diferentes regiones podrán disfrutar de esta nueva presentación del anime. Dragon Ball Super regresa con una animación mejorada Para quienes todavía no estén enterados, Dragon Ball Super: Beerus es una edición renovada del anime que se emitió originalmente entre 2015 y 2018. Toei Animation ha realizado correcciones y nuevas secuencias de animación , además de modificar efectos visuales y reorganizar parte de la historia para mejorar su presentación. Eso sí, no estamos hablando de una continuación con acontecimientos inéditos, sino de una nueva versión de las aventuras que ya conocemos. La historia comienza después de la derrota de Majin Buu, cuando Goku y sus amigos disfrutan de un periodo de tranquilidad hasta que Bills despierta de su prolongado sueño. El Dios de la Destrucción escucha rumores sobre un poderoso saiyajin y decide visitar la Tierra, provocando una serie de acontecimientos que terminarán introduciendo el Super Saiyan God y otros elementos importantes de la franquicia. Esta edición también contempla acontecimientos relacionados con la resurrección de Freezer y el torneo de Champa , recuperando algunas de las primeras sagas de Dragon Ball Super . Sin embargo, esto no significa que todos los episodios estarán disponibles con doblaje desde el primer día, pues Crunchyroll ha confirmado que su distribución será semanal. Cabe recordar que Dragon Ball Super: Beerus comenzó sus emisiones en Japón el pasado 11 de octubre, mientras que Crunchyroll ha estado ofreciendo los episodios con subtítulos para el público internacional. Ahora, con la llegada de las voces latinoamericanas, los seguidores tendrán otra oportunidad de revisitar estas batallas y comprobar qué tanto ha cambiado su apartado visual respecto a la versión original. ¿Te animarás a volver a ver las primeras sagas de Dragon Ball Super con su animación mejorada, o ya te sabes tan bien las peleas de Goku y Bills que podrías recitar sus diálogos de memoria? title: The Dangers in My Heart ya tiene fecha para su temporada 3: ¡ahora sí son novios!
summary: The Dangers in My Heart confirma el estreno de su tercera temporada para abril de 2027. Ichikawa y Yamada regresan como pareja en un nuevo tráiler.
details: Anime The Dangers in My Heart ya tiene fecha para su temporada 3: ¡ahora sí son novios! Ichikawa y Yamada regresarán como pareja en abril de 2027, mientras el manga ya llegó a su final. Ryo hace 3 horas 4 Comentarios ADS Después de dos temporadas de miradas incómodas, malentendidos y momentos que nos hicieron querer gritarles que se confesaran de una buena vez, parece que finalmente veremos cómo les va a Ichikawa y Yamada siendo novios. Se anunció oficialmente que la tercera temporada de The Dangers in My Heart se estrenará en abril de 2027 , acompañada de un nuevo tráiler y una imagen promocional que muestran a la pareja disfrutando de esta nueva etapa de su relación. La ilustración presenta a Kyotaro Ichikawa y Anna Yamada compartiendo un columpio durante el atardecer, con una frase que anuncia el comienzo de un nuevo mundo para el protagonista. Por supuesto, el avance tampoco se queda atrás, pues recupera a varios personajes conocidos y termina con Yamada anunciando que está saliendo con Ichikawa . Después de todo lo que tuvieron que pasar para llegar hasta aquí, parece que la muchacha no tiene demasiados problemas en presumir a su novio. Como recordarán los fanáticos, la segunda temporada terminó con los protagonistas convirtiéndose oficialmente en pareja. Sin embargo, conseguir novia no significa que los problemas de Ichikawa hayan terminado. Nuestro querido muchacho todavía tiene bastantes inseguridades que superar, especialmente ahora que tendrá que aprender a desenvolverse dentro de una relación sentimental. La nueva temporada abordará precisamente los primeros desafíos de su noviazgo , mientras ambos continúan con sus respectivas actividades escolares. Entre los acontecimientos que se aproximan se encuentran los exámenes de ingreso de Ichikawa, los compromisos profesionales de Yamada, un campamento de estudios y el último festival cultural de su etapa en secundaria. Así que, aunque finalmente están juntos, todavía les esperan bastantes momentos incómodos. El tráiler también muestra el regreso de Moeko Sekine, Kana Ichikawa y Akira Momoyama, además de adelantar la aparición de otros personajes que tendrán importancia durante esta etapa. La animación continuará a cargo de Shin-Ei Animation , estudio responsable de las dos temporadas anteriores, con Hiroaki Akagi como director general y Dali Chen en la dirección. Cabe recordar que The Dangers in My Heart , conocido en Japón como Boku no Kokoro no Yabai Yatsu , estrenó su primera temporada en abril de 2023, seguida de una segunda entrega en enero de 2024. La franquicia también llegó a los cines con The Dangers in My Heart: The Movie , una película estrenada en febrero de 2026 que recopiló acontecimientos del anime e incorporó escenas adicionales. Su distribución incluyó países como México, Estados Unidos, Francia y Alemania. El manga de The Dangers in My Heart ya terminó Por otra parte, la noticia llega poco después de que el manga original de Norio Sakurai concluyera su publicación el pasado 15 de septiembre, poniendo fin a más de ocho años de serialización. La obra comenzó en marzo de 2018 dentro de la revista Weekly Shonen Champion de Akita Shoten, antes de trasladarse a la plataforma digital Champion Cross . Su decimocuarto y último volumen tiene programado su lanzamiento para el 6 de noviembre en Japón. Eso sí, el final del manga no significa que la franquicia vaya a desaparecer. Además de la tercera temporada, la historia cuenta con una novela ligera escrita por Kota Nozomi y un manga derivado titulado The Dangers in My Heart: A Romantic Comedy Will Not Start . Por ahora, el anime todavía no tiene una fecha exacta de estreno más allá de abril de 2027. ¿Te emociona ver a Ichikawa y Yamada enfrentándose a sus primeros problemas como novios, o crees que el pobre Kyotaro seguirá poniéndose nervioso cada vez que Anna se le acerque demasiado? title: Chamomile niega vender citas a sus fans y ahora va tras 60 cuentas que difundieron el rumor
summary: La cosplayer japonesa Chamomile negó rumores sobre citas pagadas y presentó una denuncia. Su agencia busca identificar 60 cuentas y propone acuerdos de 110,000 yenes.
details: Cultura Otaku Chamomile niega vender citas a sus fans y ahora va tras 60 cuentas que difundieron el rumor La cosplayer japonesa presentó una denuncia y su agencia ofrece acuerdos de 110,000 yenes a quienes difundieron las acusaciones. Ryo hace 34 minutos 0 Comentarios ADS Compartir rumores sobre una cosplayer puede parecer inofensivo para algunos usuarios de internet, pero esta vez las cosas podrían terminar en los tribunales. La popular cosplayer japonesa Chamomile negó las acusaciones que circulaban sobre supuestas citas privadas a cambio de dinero y, lejos de dejar pasar el asunto, presentó una denuncia penal contra la persona a la que responsabiliza de iniciar los rumores. De acuerdo con la versión difundida por su agencia, las acusaciones fueron inventadas por una mujer que habría actuado por resentimiento personal. La representación de Chamomile sostiene que la información compartida en redes sociales es falsa y que su difusión ha perjudicado la reputación de la creadora de contenido. Por ahora, estas afirmaciones corresponden a la postura de la cosplayer y su equipo, sin que se haya anunciado una resolución judicial sobre el conflicto. Sin embargo, las acciones legales no estarían dirigidas únicamente contra la persona señalada como responsable de iniciar la controversia. La agencia también decidió investigar a quienes ayudaron a propagar las publicaciones, incluso cuando no fueron sus autores originales. Hasta compartir rumores con emojis podría tener consecuencias Según la información divulgada por su representación, se han iniciado procedimientos para identificar a aproximadamente 60 cuentas que habrían contribuido a difundir las acusaciones. La revisión contempla publicaciones que utilizaron determinadas palabras clave e incluso emojis para hacer referencia al caso, por lo que la investigación no se limitaría a los mensajes que mencionaron directamente a Chamomile. Eso sí, la agencia también ofreció una alternativa antes de considerar demandas individuales. Los responsables de las publicaciones señaladas podrían solicitar un acuerdo mediante una disculpa por escrito y el pago de 110,000 yenes , equivalentes a unos 696 dólares según la cifra difundida. Se trata de una propuesta de conciliación de carácter privado, no de una multa impuesta por las autoridades. La situación ha llamado la atención por el alcance de las medidas anunciadas. Aunque una persona no haya inventado un rumor, compartirlo o contribuir a su difusión también puede generar conflictos legales dependiendo del contenido publicado y de las circunstancias. No obstante, esto tampoco significa que utilizar un emoji o comentar una controversia constituya automáticamente un delito. Por ahora, no se ha informado cuántas de las cuentas señaladas han sido identificadas, si alguna persona aceptó el acuerdo económico o si se presentarán demandas adicionales. Chamomile y su representación mantienen su rechazo a las acusaciones y buscan evitar que continúen circulando como si fueran hechos comprobados. ¿Crees que quienes comparten rumores sin comprobarlos deberían enfrentar las mismas consecuencias que la persona que los inventó, o existe una diferencia importante entre ambas responsabilidades? title: Discord habría cerrado un servidor de To Love-Ru y baneado hasta a sus miembros silenciosos
summary: Discord habría eliminado un servidor de To Love-Ru con nueve años de actividad y suspendido cuentas de usuarios que aseguran no haber publicado contenido.
details: Anime Discord habría cerrado un servidor de To Love-Ru y baneado hasta a sus miembros silenciosos La comunidad llevaba nueve años activa y varios usuarios denuncian suspensiones permanentes sin haber publicado mensajes. Aiko hace 5 horas 1 Comentarios ADS Imagínate entrar a un servidor de Discord para seguir las novedades de tu anime favorito, olvidarte de que estás allí y descubrir años después que tu cuenta fue suspendida por pertenecer a esa comunidad. Pues algo parecido habrían experimentado varios seguidores de To Love-Ru , después de que Discord eliminara un servidor dedicado a la franquicia que llevaba aproximadamente nueve años funcionando. Lo más polémico es que las sanciones también habrían alcanzado a usuarios que nunca participaron activamente en las conversaciones. La situación comenzó a llamar la atención después de que varios afectados compartieran sus experiencias en redes sociales. Según explicó una usuaria conocida como Ayaka, el servidor reunía a seguidores del manga y anime de Kentaro Yabuki y Saki Hasemi, pero terminó siendo eliminado por presuntas infracciones relacionadas con las políticas de seguridad infantil de Discord. Entre los contenidos cuestionados habría ilustraciones de personajes de la franquicia, incluyendo imágenes generadas mediante inteligencia artificial. Sin embargo, las suspensiones no se habrían limitado a quienes compartieron imágenes . De acuerdo con los testimonios, algunas personas recibieron restricciones o perdieron permanentemente sus cuentas pese a no haber publicado mensajes ni archivos dentro del servidor. Esto provocó numerosas quejas de usuarios que consideraban injusto recibir una sanción por contenido que no habían compartido personalmente. El asunto tampoco habría terminado después de presentar las reclamaciones correspondientes. Según los afectados, varios usuarios solicitaron que Discord revisara sus suspensiones, argumentando que no habían participado en las publicaciones que motivaron el cierre. Sin embargo, las apelaciones habrían sido rechazadas , manteniendo las sanciones incluso después de una nueva revisión. Cabe señalar que las propias normas de Discord contemplan medidas contra comunidades donde se comparta contenido prohibido. La plataforma también explica que, en casos graves, los integrantes de un servidor pueden recibir infracciones relacionadas con las actividades de la comunidad. Eso sí, no se ha podido confirmar públicamente qué publicaciones concretas provocaron el cierre del servidor de To Love-Ru ni cuántas cuentas terminaron suspendidas. El caso ha generado discusiones entre seguidores del anime sobre las responsabilidades de los administradores y de los usuarios que simplemente pertenecen a una comunidad. Mientras algunos consideran necesario que Discord mantenga controles estrictos sobre el contenido compartido, otros cuestionan que las sanciones puedan alcanzar a personas que nunca participaron en las infracciones denunciadas. ¿Crees que Discord debería castigar únicamente a quienes publican contenido prohibido, o pertenecer a un servidor problemático también debería tener consecuencias para los demás integrantes? title: Ado visito México por BTS y la altura la dejó buscando oxígeno para respirar
summary: Ado contó que la altura de la Ciudad de México la obligó a buscar oxígeno durante su viaje para ver a BTS. También reveló que se volvió fan de Jimin.
details: Anime Ado visito México por BTS y la altura la dejó buscando oxígeno para respirar La cantante japonesa contó que necesitó oxígeno en la CDMX y que terminó enamorada de Jimin de BTS. Ryo hace 13 segundos 0 Comentarios ADS La Ciudad de México tiene una manera bastante particular de recibir a sus visitantes, y parece que ni las estrellas japonesas se salvan. La cantante Ado reveló que durante su viaje a México para asistir a un concierto de BTS terminó necesitando oxígeno debido a la altura de la capital. Lo curioso es que, pese a semejante experiencia, regresó a Japón con un nuevo integrante favorito del grupo surcoreano: Jimin. La anécdota salió a la luz durante un evento exclusivo para su club de fans celebrado el pasado 25 de octubre en Tokio. Según los asistentes, Ado estaba contando algunas de las cosas que había aprendido durante sus viajes internacionales cuando recordó que en México prácticamente se había quedado sin aire. La cantante explicó que, después de pasar dos o tres días en la capital mexicana, comenzó a experimentar molestias similares al mal de altura. La situación llegó a ser tan incómoda que, según los relatos de los asistentes, necesitaba inhalar oxígeno entre frases para poder terminar de hablar . Su equipo tuvo que buscar un establecimiento que ofreciera este servicio durante las 24 horas del día. Y aunque para muchos mexicanos pueda parecer una exageración, la situación tiene una explicación. La Ciudad de México se encuentra aproximadamente a 2,240 metros sobre el nivel del mar , una altura considerable para quienes están acostumbrados a vivir en ciudades mucho más cercanas al nivel del mar, como Tokio. La menor presión atmosférica puede dificultar la adaptación de algunos visitantes y provocar síntomas como dolor de cabeza, cansancio o dificultad para respirar. Pero no todo fueron problemas respiratorios. La cantante también contó que había viajado a México para disfrutar de uno de los conciertos de BTS, que se presentó en el Estadio GNP Seguros los días 7, 9 y 10 de mayo de 2026 como parte de su gira mundial. Y aunque Ado también sabe perfectamente lo que significa estar sobre un escenario, esta vez le tocó vivir la experiencia desde el público. Según los asistentes al evento de su club de fans, después del concierto quedó especialmente impresionada con Jimin , hasta el punto de convertirse en una de sus admiradoras. Además, reveló que todavía guarda en su cartera un llavero artesanal del cantante que le regaló otra persona durante su visita al concierto. Este último detalle llamó particularmente la atención de los seguidores de BTS, ya que el intercambio de pequeños regalos entre fanáticos es una costumbre bastante conocida dentro de la comunidad ARMY. Por lo visto, Ado no solamente se llevó una buena experiencia musical de México, sino también un recuerdo que continúa conservando meses después de su visita. Eso sí, conviene aclarar que la historia fue difundida por personas que asistieron al evento privado de la cantante, por lo que los detalles sobre el uso de oxígeno proceden de sus testimonios y no de un comunicado médico. Lo que sí está confirmado es que BTS realizó sus tres conciertos en la capital mexicana durante mayo. ¿Qué te sorprendió más: que Ado viniera hasta México solamente para ver a BTS, que la altura de la CDMX la dejara sin aire o que terminara guardando un llaverito de Jimin en su cartera? title: Dragon Ball Z composer elected Texas Attorney General
summary: A former Dragon Ball Z composer has been elected Texas Attorney General in a shocking upset.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 TV & Movies Anime Dragon Ball Z composer elected Texas Attorney General by Michael Gwilliam Published: Nov 04, 2026, 18:30 Save for later Save for later Facebook/Toei Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News A former Dragon Ball Z composer has been elected Texas Attorney General, marking an unlikely career transformation from creating music for Goku and Vegeta to becoming the state’s top lawyer. Democrat Nathan Johnson defeated Republican Mayes Middleton in the November 3 election, marking the first time in 32 years that a Democrat has been elected Texas Attorney General, with Dan Morales being the last to win the office in 1994. Johnson, who has served in the Texas Senate since 2019, will take office in January 2027, replacing outgoing Attorney General Ken Paxton. Article continues after ad While his election is a major political upset, anime fans might recognize Johnson’s name from an entirely different career. Before entering politics, Johnson worked as a composer for Funimation’s English dub of Dragon Ball Z, providing music for the first 67 episodes of the 2005 Ultimate Uncut edition. He also contributed music to five Dragon Ball Z movies, including Broly: Second Coming, Fusion Reborn, and Wrath of the Dragon. Article continues after ad Dragon Ball fans help power Nathan Johnson to victory In a 2012 interview with The Dao of Dragon Ball , Johnson revealed that he had never watched the anime before being hired and initially struggled to connect with its characters and story. Article continues after ad Crunchyroll However, he eventually developed an appreciation for the series, particularly through Gohan, whose relationship with his father resonated with Johnson as a parent. His connection to Dragon Ball Z even became part of his political identity when he first ran for the Texas Senate in 2018. Speaking to The Dao of Dragon Ball following that election victory, Johnson revealed that younger voters were surprised to discover his anime background. “Along the way some of them found out about my music background, and specifically about Dragon Ball Z, and they got really excited about it,” he explained. Article continues after ad Dragon Ball has also found its way into politics elsewhere. As Dexerto previously reported , former Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba once appeared at a public event dressed as Majin Buu. details: The site with a goal of “Adding muscles to everyday life” has released a new gallery collecting its most viral muscly moments up to the present . Fukuoka-based Smile Academy’s Muscle Plus free stock image site has been around for a while now and it hasn’t stopped causing a stir. We can only thank the muscular geniuses who decided to gift the world with free-to-use, professional-quality shots of themselves posing in situations that make you think, “Heck, I can’t use that for anything!” before immediately downloading it anyway. Their purpose is not only making viewers’ smile muscles move but also promoting local people, cultural artifacts, events, and places in rural Fukuoka Prefecture in an effort to revitalize the area. Much of their work is seasonally appropriate as well, as seen in the epic Halloween photo story collection a few years back . ▼ Logo for the Muscle Plus free stock image site Thanks to the positive public response, Muscle Plus has just released a new page that collects the photos and some quantitative data behind its most trending photos on Twitter. Thanks to this new system, you can simply check out which photos are getting the most hits when you’re in need of an image with impact. Below, we’ve compiled five of the top trending photos along with the date when they were uploaded to Twitter and their cumulative likes and views. All numbers are accurate as of October 21, 2026, so many have likely gained more hits since then. 1. Uploaded to Twitter on September 26, 2026 123,553 likes / 9,337,570 views There’s nothing quite as refreshing as two buff dudes frolicking in a field of vibrantly pink cosmos in Nokonoshima Park. This would be a peak tourism campaign if we ever saw one. 2. Uploaded October 1, 2026 52,535 likes / 2,170,577 views Two guys demonstrate how to harvest tea leaves at Yame Central Tea Plantation. Uploaded July 18, 2025 94,684 likes / 3,594,236 views This quintessential summertime shot in the sunflower field at Fukufuku no Sato farmers’ market reminds us that it’s OK to stop and sniff the flowers–sans shirts–sometimes. 4. Uploaded December 25, 2022 14,419 likes / 846,854 views We just hate it when we’re baking in the kitchen at Patisserie Serenite and someone comes along and sneakily adds liquid protein to the freshly whipped cream we were making. Thank goodness there’s a stock image to capture that situation. The dudes at Muscle Plus have almost gotten us excited enough to start our own library of free stock images–though in our case, there would be much less of the buff and more of the puff . title: Starbucks Japan reveals this year’s lucky bag, but you’ll have to act fast to get one
summary: Fukubukuro season starts very early for Starbucks fans in Japan. In Japan, shops, restaurants, and other companies celebrate the new year by releasing fukubukuro, a.k.a. lucky bags, surprise assortments of their wares and coupons, usually with a combined value much greater than their asking price. Back in the day, the only way to get a […]
details: Fukubukuro season starts very early for Starbucks fans in Japan . In Japan, shops, restaurants, and other companies celebrate the new year by releasing fukubukuro , a.k.a. lucky bags , surprise assortments of their wares and coupons, usually with a combined value much greater than their asking price. Back in the day, the only way to get a lucky bag was to show up at the shop on the first few days of the year, but especially popular bags now go on sale ahead of time, and with Starbucks Japan’s lucky bag being one of the most popular of all, it’s going on sale while we’re still in November . One of the reasons Starbucks Japan’s lucky bag is so coveted is because of the bag itself . While most other brands’ fukubukuro are disposable paper pouches, Starbucks Japan gives you a classy tote bag . The design, featuring an emblem of the Starbucks mermaid, is elegantly understated in order to coordinate with a wide variety of outfits, and sized such that it can work for both fashionable in-city meetups or more extensive outings for which you need to carry more gear. But you can’t be a lucky bag without also having cool stuff inside. The highlight of the contents is a fukubukuro-exclusive Starbucks Japan stainless steel drink bottle , the design of which is still being kept under wraps. You’ll also receive three pieces of randomly selected Starbucks lucky bag-exclusive merch , which could be one of 1,000 special mug and Bearista plushie combos. ▼ The surprise is super lucky and super cute. To fill up the drink bottle, the bag additionally contains two bags of Starbucks coffee , one of high-grade roast and one of light-note blend, as well as a Coffee Bean Ticket redeemable for a bag of coffee of up to 2,000 yen (US$13) at any Starbucks Japan branch. Finally, for when you’re not in the mood to do your own brewing, the bundle also contains seven drink tickets , once again redeemable at any Starbucks in Japan. The 2027 Starbucks lucky bag is priced at 9,500 yen, but because the demand is so high for them every year, it’s offered by a pre-sale lottery system only. To enter, you’ll need to be a My Starbucks member and complete the online entry form between November 4 and November 15 . Randomly selected winners will then be notified by email (Starbucks says notifications are slated to be sent out by November 25), after which payment can be arranged and you can select a delivery date between January 1 and 7 of 2027 (domestic shipping is included in the price of the fukubukuro). The entry form can be found here . And if it’s still too early for you to be thinking about New Year’s, but not too early for you to be thinking about Christmas, Starbucks Japan has something for you too . title: Thief mails 460 million-yen watch back to Tokyo store he stole it from, says “I’m sorry”
summary: Latest crook to hit Tokyo’s hottest theft target feels either remorse or fear, but probably shouldn’t expect forgiveness. In a city as big as Tokyo, different neighborhoods have different atmospheres, but those reputations can change over time. For example, Nakano is best known for its Nakano Broadway shopping center, which used to be thought of […]
details: Latest crook to hit Tokyo’s hottest theft target feels either remorse or fear, but probably shouldn’t expect forgiveness . In a city as big as Tokyo , different neighborhoods have different atmospheres, but those reputations can change over time. For example, Nakano is best known for its Nakano Broadway shopping center, which used to be thought of almost entirely as a place for fans of eclectic pop and subculture genres, sort of like a weirder, less trendy version of Akihabara. Over the last few years, though, Nakano Broadway has become famous for having a dense concentration of luxury wristwatch stores, stocked with both new and used high-demand models . Sadly, Nakano Broadway’s reputation is continuing to evolve, and it’s now becoming a place known for attracting not only watch fans, but watch thieves too . On the evening of October 29, a man, at the time seemingly an interested shopper, approached a salesperson inside a watch store in Nakano Broadway and asked if he could try on a piece that was in a locked showcase. The salesperson obliged, and the man slipped on a watch from Swiss brand Audemars Piguet, only to suddenly run off with it still on his wrist. And while the man hadn’t been an actual shopper, he apparently still knew a thing or two about watches, as the model he stole has a price of 46 million yen (approximately US$290,000). ▼ A CG reenactment of the crime After fleeing the building, the man escaped out into the web of narrow streets that twist around Nakano Broadway. However, this is still a fairly developed part of Tokyo, not the sort of place where a sprinting thief can blend in with fitness joggers, but Nakano also isn’t so dense one can easily disappear into a sea of passersby either. As a result, investigators were able to spot the fleeing man in recording from multiple security cameras , as shown in the video here. ▼ The video also shows the model of watch that was stolen. Though the thief is still at large (as of this writing), the stolen watch has been returned, and, surprisingly, it was the thief himself who returned it, via a takuhaibin/parcel delivery service . On the morning of November 1, a cardboard box which had been mailed from Aichi Prefecture was delivered to the store that was robbed, and when the staff opened it, they found a watch matching the model and serial number of the one that was stolen, plus a handwritten letter of apology that included the statement “I’m sorry.” The watch doesn’t appear to have suffered any noticeable damage during its time away from the store. Online reactions to the unexpected turn of events have included: “Must have realized it was only a matter of time until they caught him.” “Okay, so he got spooked and returned the watch. He still stole it.” “Returning it doesn’t undo the crime. Turn yourself in.” “It’s like he thinks they’ll just treat it as a prank since he the watch back.” “If you know you should return it, you should have known not to take it in the first place.” “Thieves have totally marked Nakano Broadway.” “If they’re going to let people try on watches that are that expensive, they should make them do it in a locked room.” With law-abiding citizens in Japan still fuming over a different brazen watch robbery that recently took place at Nakano Broadway , it’s not surprising that public sentiment isn’t leaning towards letting the guy off the hook just because he returned the property that he stole. Japan is, after all, the country that says “If everything could be solved by saying ‘sorry,’ we wouldn’t need police,” and investigators are still searching for the thief.
