title: Mercedes and the Waning Moon: ser vampira tampoco te salva de la pobreza
summary: Mercedes and the Waning Moon revela un nuevo tráiler y cuatro actores de voz. El anime de la pequeña vampira se estrenará en enero de 2027.
details: Anime Mercedes and the Waning Moon: ser vampira tampoco te salva de la pobreza El anime de fantasía y reencarnación presenta un nuevo tráiler y suma a las voces de My Hero Academia, Jujutsu Kaisen y KonoSuba a su elenco. Ryo hace 1 hora 1 Comentarios ADS Reencarnar como una vampira y nacer en una familia noble debería ser suficiente para tener la vida resuelta, ¿verdad? Pues parece que a Mercedes Grunewald no le tocó tanta suerte. La adaptación al anime de Mercedes and the Waning Moon: The Dungeoneering Feats of a Discarded Vampire Aristocrat ha presentado su segundo tráiler promocional , acompañado de la incorporación de cuatro nuevos actores de voz. La serie tiene programado su estreno para enero de 2027 en la televisión japonesa. El avance muestra nuevas escenas de combate y permite escuchar por primera vez a varios de los personajes que acompañarán a Mercedes durante sus aventuras. Entre las incorporaciones destacan Kenta Miyake, conocido por interpretar a All Might en My Hero Academia , y Junichi Suwabe, la voz de Ryomen Sukuna en Jujutsu Kaisen . Así que, por lo menos en cuanto a las voces, esta pequeña vampira estará bastante bien acompañada. Una vampira que tendrá que ganarse la vida desde niña La historia sigue a Mercedes Grunewald, una mujer que murió sin haber encontrado un verdadero propósito en su vida y que terminó reencarnando como una pequeña vampira en una familia aristocrática. El problema es que su padre tiene otras prioridades y, tarde o temprano, elegirá a un heredero que no será ella. Para empeorar las cosas, su madre es una concubina marginada, la familia carece de recursos y tampoco cuentan con demasiadas personas que puedan ayudarlas. Ante semejante panorama, Mercedes encuentra una solución bastante peculiar: explorar calabozos para ganar dinero . Después de todo, en este mundo cualquiera puede convertirse en explorador, incluso una niña que apenas tiene edad para asistir al jardín de niños. Aprovechando las habilidades que posee como vampira, comenzará a entrenar desde muy pequeña para mantener a su familia y asegurarse de que su segunda vida no termine siendo tan decepcionante como la primera. Sin embargo, convertirse en una exploradora no será tan sencillo como esperaba. Los calabozos esconden monstruos peligrosos y misterios que Mercedes tendrá que descubrir mientras aumenta sus habilidades. El nuevo avance también presenta a algunos de sus futuros compañeros, incluyendo a Benkei, una criatura de seis brazos, y Kuro, un monstruo con apariencia de lobo que terminará convirtiéndose en uno de sus aliados. El anime suma voces de Jujutsu Kaisen y KonoSuba En cuanto al elenco de voces, se confirmó que Anna Nagase interpretará a Mercedes Grunewald , actriz conocida por dar vida a Ushio Kofune en Summer Time Rendering . Los cuatro integrantes adicionales anunciados son los siguientes: Benkei: Kenta Miyake, conocido por interpretar a All Might en My Hero Academia . Kuro: Ryunosuke Watanuki, quien anteriormente dio voz a Okuhito Iemon en Blue Lock . Florian: Junichi Suwabe, reconocido por interpretar a Ryomen Sukuna en Jujutsu Kaisen . Ryudia Grunewald: Ai Kayano, la voz de Darkness en KonoSuba: God's Blessing on This Wonderful World! . Entre los nuevos personajes también destaca Florian, un trabajador del gremio de exploradores que mostrará un interés particular por las actividades de Mercedes. De hecho, el propio Junichi Suwabe dejó en el aire si su personaje será realmente un aliado o si terminará traicionando a la protagonista, por lo que habrá que estar atentos a sus verdaderas intenciones. Respecto al equipo de producción, Kunihisa Sugishima estará a cargo de la dirección en los estudios Teddy, mientras que Jun Kumagai se encargará de la composición de la serie. Los diseños de personajes estarán a cargo de Nami Shoyama, con R.O.N y Shuhei Mutsuki responsables de la música. Cabe recordar que la historia original, escrita por Firehead, comenzó a publicarse en el portal Shosetsuka ni Narou en 2018, antes de recibir una edición como novela ligera bajo el sello TO Books, con ilustraciones de KeG, en 2021. Ese mismo año también comenzó una adaptación al manga ilustrada por Pochi Edoya. La serie es conocida en Japón bajo el título de Kaketa Tsuki no Mercedes . ¿Te llama la atención ver a una pequeña vampira enfrentándose a monstruos para sacar adelante a su familia, o ya estás saturado de historias de reencarnaciones? title: Pole Princess!! vuelve al cine en 2027, pero solo por dos semanas
summary: Pole Princess!!: Croix du Nord llegará a los cines japoneses el 29 de enero de 2027. Conoce su historia, nueva protagonista y elenco de voces.
details: Anime Pole Princess!! vuelve al cine en 2027, pero solo por dos semanas La franquicia de pole dance estrenará Croix du Nord, una nueva producción de 60 minutos con cinco canciones y una misteriosa chica que se unirá a la historia. Aiko hace 2 horas 0 Comentarios ADS Las chicas de Pole Princess!! todavía tienen algunas coreografías pendientes y, por lo visto, no piensan abandonar los escenarios tan pronto. Avex Pictures y Tatsunoko Production anunciaron una nueva película titulada Pole Princess!!: Croix du Nord , que llegará a los cines japoneses el próximo 29 de enero de 2027. Sin embargo, quienes quieran disfrutar de este espectáculo en pantalla grande tendrán que apresurarse, pues solamente estará disponible durante dos semanas en seis salas de Japón. La nueva producción tendrá una duración aproximada de 60 minutos de animación CG y contará con cinco canciones incluidas en el álbum Shining Pole Song Album , lanzado en febrero de 2026. Además de presentar nuevas actuaciones de pole dance, la película continuará los acontecimientos de la entrega cinematográfica de 2023 e introducirá a una chica que parece tener una conexión bastante particular con una de las protagonistas. Una nueva rival aparece en Pole Princess!! La historia comenzará después de los acontecimientos de la Pole Dance Japan Cup, donde Hinano Hoshikita y sus compañeras de Galaxy Princess se enfrentaron al poderoso grupo Aile d'Ange. Ahora que la competencia ha terminado, las cuatro chicas continúan perfeccionando sus habilidades y explorando nuevas formas de presentarse sobre el escenario. Todo cambia cuando Yukari Mikoshiro, integrante del grupo rival, las contacta para invitarlas a participar como artistas especiales en un evento organizado por Aile d'Ange. Las protagonistas aceptan encantadas, aunque la verdadera sorpresa llegará cuando una misteriosa joven llamada Luchika Himeori aparezca repentinamente en el estudio de Azumi. Por ahora, los responsables no han explicado demasiado sobre esta nueva integrante, pero adelantaron que tiene una relación importante con Azumi. Su diseño original estuvo a cargo del ilustrador tomari, quien también participó en la creación de los personajes de la franquicia. Habrá que ver si su aparición termina complicando las cosas para las chicas o si simplemente tendremos a otra apasionada del pole dance. El elenco de voces regresará para la película En cuanto al elenco, se confirmó el regreso de las ocho actrices de voz principales de la franquicia, incluyendo a varias figuras bastante conocidas dentro de la industria del anime: Hinano Hoshikita: Rio Tsuchiya, quien también interpretó a Mei Toomi en CUE! . Lilia Saijo: Anna Suzuki, conocida por interpretar a Lemon Kokoa en Waccha PriMagi! . Mio Tousaka: Yui Ogura, quien dio voz a Hinata Hakamada en Ro-Kyu-Bu! . Subaru Nanyo: Minami Hinata, reconocida por interpretar a Bojji en Ranking of Kings . Yukari Mikoshiro: Yoshino Nanjo, quien interpretó a Eli Ayase en Love Live! School Idol Project . Sana Murafuji: Rina Hidaka, conocida por dar voz a Milim Nava en That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime . Noa Aoi: Saori Hayami, quien interpreta a Yor Forger en SPY x FAMILY . Azumi Shino: Rie Kugimiya, la inolvidable voz de Taiga Aisaka en Toradora! . Por otra parte, Hitomi Ezoe regresará a la dirección en Tatsunoko Production, acompañada nuevamente por Toko Machida en los guiones y Yoshihiro Otobe en la dirección de animación CG. Kotono Sakurai se encargará de adaptar los diseños de personajes para la animación, mientras que Kenta Higashiohji compondrá la música. Las coreografías también contarán con la supervisión de KAORI, de Studio Transform, quien ha participado en el proyecto desde sus inicios. Cabe recordar que Pole Princess!! comenzó como una serie original distribuida por internet entre finales de 2022 y principios de 2023. Su historia sigue a Hinano Hoshikita, una estudiante que descubre el pole dance y termina formando un grupo junto a sus amigas. La franquicia estrenó su primera película en noviembre de 2023, con una competencia que enfrentó a Galaxy Princess contra las experimentadas integrantes de Aile d'Ange. De momento, no se ha confirmado un estreno internacional para Pole Princess!!: Croix du Nord , por lo que los fanáticos fuera de Japón tendrán que esperar nuevas noticias sobre su distribución. ¿Te gustaría ver esta nueva película de Pole Princess!! , o preferirías que las chicas regresaran con una temporada completa en lugar de otro estreno cinematográfico? title: Death Stranding Isolations muestra un tráiler inquietante: «Mi mamá se convirtió en un cráter»
summary: Death Stranding Isolations revela un inquietante tráiler, detalles de su historia y equipo creativo. El anime de Hideo Kojima llegará a Disney+ en 2027.
details: Anime Death Stranding Isolations muestra un tráiler inquietante: «Mi mamá se convirtió en un cráter» El anime de Hideo Kojima llegará a Disney+ en 2027 y contará una historia original ambientada después de los acontecimientos del primer videojuego. Kudasai hace 2 horas 4 Comentarios ADS El mundo de Hideo Kojima todavía tiene muchas historias perturbadoras por contar, y parece que la próxima llegará en forma de anime. Kojima Productions publicó un nuevo tráiler de Death Stranding Isolations , acompañado de una imagen promocional y más detalles sobre la historia y el equipo de producción. La serie, que utilizará animación tradicional en 2D, tiene previsto su estreno en Disney+ durante 2027 . El avance se presentó durante un evento por el décimo aniversario de Kojima Productions en Japón, y esta vez el protagonismo se lo lleva una joven que ha decidido darle la espalda al resto de la humanidad. Y es que, si sobrevivir en el mundo de Death Stranding ya era suficientemente complicado, parece que reconectar a las personas tampoco ha solucionado todos sus problemas. Una historia donde la soledad será protagonista La nueva sinopsis comienza con una frase bastante inquietante: "Mi mamá se convirtió en un cráter". La joven que pronuncia estas palabras perdió a su madre durante el fenómeno conocido como Death Stranding, cuando el contacto entre los vivos y los muertos provocó una serie de explosiones catastróficas. Desde entonces, ha vivido completamente aislada, hasta acostumbrarse tanto a la soledad que ya no desea relacionarse con nadie. Los acontecimientos se desarrollarán después de que Sam Bridges reconectara Norteamérica mediante la Red Quiral. Sin embargo, la historia no seguirá directamente al protagonista de los videojuegos, sino a otros sobrevivientes que han decidido tomar caminos diferentes. Entre ellos se encuentran un anciano que intenta conectar a las personas mediante métodos poco convencionales, una soldado atrapada en un ciclo interminable de violencia y un muchacho lleno de resentimiento hacia su propia existencia. Por supuesto, la joven protagonista tampoco podrá mantenerse alejada del mundo para siempre. Una serie de encuentros inesperados terminará sacándola de su aislamiento, obligándola a conocer una realidad que durante mucho tiempo había preferido ignorar. La producción contará una historia independiente de los videojuegos, aunque conservará el mismo universo y sus particulares reglas. Veteranos de Attack on Titan y Psycho-Pass trabajarán en el anime En cuanto al equipo creativo, Takayuki Sano estará a cargo de la dirección en los estudios E&H production, conocidos por trabajos como Ninja Kamui y Bullet/Bullet . Sano también participó como director de animación de episodios de Attack on Titan: The Final Season , mientras que Hideo Kojima se desempeñará como productor ejecutivo. Por otra parte, Tow Ubukata escribirá los guiones y se encargará de la composición de la serie. El escritor es conocido por sus novelas de Mardock Scramble , además de haber trabajado en producciones como Ghost in the Shell: Arise , Fafner y Psycho-Pass 2 . Los diseños originales de personajes estarán a cargo de Ilya Kuvshinov, quien anteriormente participó en Ghost in the Shell: SAC_2045 , con Sayaka Koiso encargada de adaptarlos para la animación. Sobre su participación, Sano explicó que asumió el proyecto con un fuerte sentido de responsabilidad, pues considera que las obras de Kojima tienen una capacidad especial para conectar emocionalmente con quienes las disfrutan. El director también señaló que quería conseguir algo similar con esta adaptación, que será realizada mediante animación 2D dibujada a mano . Cabe recordar que esta no será la única adaptación de la franquicia. Kojima Productions también tiene en desarrollo Death Stranding Mosquito , una película animada con una historia independiente, además de un largometraje de imagen real. Por ahora, Death Stranding Isolations continúa sin una fecha exacta de estreno y tampoco se ha revelado su elenco de voces. ¿Crees que Sam Bridges terminará apareciendo en esta nueva historia, o prefieres que el pobre repartidor descanse de una vez por todas? title: Kuromi se adueña de la pantalla grande: tendrá su primera película en 2027
summary: Kuromi tendrá su primera película como protagonista en 2027. Sanrio presentó el proyecto durante Halloween y reveló sus primeros detalles.
details: Anime Kuromi se adueña de la pantalla grande: tendrá su primera película en 2027 Sanrio anunció el primer largometraje protagonizado por la popular rival de My Melody, aprovechando Halloween para celebrar su cumpleaños por todo lo alto. Aiko hace 10 segundos 0 Comentarios ADS Después de tantos años siendo la autoproclamada rival de My Melody, parece que finalmente le llegó el momento de quedarse con todos los reflectores. Sanrio anunció que Kuromi tendrá su primera película como protagonista , con un estreno programado para 2027 en los cines de Japón. La noticia se dio a conocer el pasado 31 de octubre, aprovechando Halloween y, por supuesto, el cumpleaños de la pequeña alborotadora que se ha convertido en uno de los personajes más populares de la compañía. El anuncio estuvo acompañado de una imagen promocional y un video especial en el que la propia Kuromi celebra que finalmente tendrá su película. Incluso su inseparable compañero Baku aparece para felicitarla, mientras que ella aprovecha para agradecer a sus seguidores, conocidos como los KUROMIES, por todo el apoyo que ha recibido. Por ahora, la película no tiene una fecha exacta de estreno , aunque se confirmó que la distribuidora GAGA se encargará de llevarla a los cines japoneses. En cuanto a la historia, Sanrio todavía no ha revelado una sinopsis ni los responsables de la producción, por lo que tendremos que esperar para descubrir qué clase de problemas terminará causando Kuromi en su aventura cinematográfica. Tampoco se ha confirmado si My Melody tendrá alguna participación, aunque sería bastante curioso ver una película de su eterna rival sin que ambas terminaran cruzándose en algún momento. Kuromi ha recorrido un largo camino desde su debut Aunque actualmente es uno de los rostros más reconocibles de Sanrio, Kuromi no comenzó su trayectoria como parte de una línea independiente de productos. Su primera aparición fue en el anime Onegai My Melody , estrenado en abril de 2005, donde fue presentada como la rival de la adorable conejita. Su personalidad rebelde, su capucha negra y el característico cráneo rosa terminaron convirtiéndola en una favorita de muchos seguidores. Y vaya que ha conseguido hacerse un nombre. En la edición de 2026 del Sanrio Character Ranking , Kuromi consiguió el cuarto puesto de popularidad , manteniéndose entre los cinco personajes más votados de la compañía. Su popularidad también le permitió protagonizar los cortos animados de Kuromi's Pretty Journey en 2023 y 2024, además de compartir pantalla con su eterna rival en My Melody & Kuromi , la serie de animación stop-motion estrenada en Netflix durante julio de 2025. Por si fuera poco, en octubre de 2025 también debutó oficialmente como artista musical bajo el nombre de KUROMI, a través del sello TOY'S FACTORY. Ahora dará el salto a los cines con su primer largometraje, aunque todavía no hay noticias sobre un estreno internacional . Sanrio aseguró que compartirá información sobre otros países y territorios cuando se concreten los planes de distribución. ¿Crees que Kuromi conseguirá brillar por su cuenta en la pantalla grande, o sería un desperdicio no incluir a My Melody para que ambas vuelvan a pelearse como en los viejos tiempos? title: La creadora de A Couple of Cuckoos prepara un anime de vampiras y romance
summary: La creadora de A Couple of Cuckoos anuncia el anime de Hiragi-san's House of Vampires, una comedia romántica sobre una familia de vampiros.
details: Anime La creadora de A Couple of Cuckoos prepara un anime de vampiras y romance Hiragi-san's House of Vampires tendrá una adaptación televisiva sobre un joven que termina viviendo con una familia de vampiros. ¿Qué podría salir mal? Kudasai hace 33 minutos 2 Comentarios ADS Conseguir una familia adoptiva debería ser motivo de felicidad, pero probablemente nadie le advirtió a Shota Minamoto que sus nuevos parientes tendrían cierta afición por la sangre humana. Se anunció oficialmente que Hiragi-san's House of Vampires tendrá una adaptación al anime , basada en el manga de Miki Yoshikawa, la reconocida autora de A Couple of Cuckoos y Yamada-kun and the Seven Witches . El anuncio llegó acompañado de una primera imagen promocional que deja bastante claras las intenciones de una de sus protagonistas. La ilustración muestra a Yukie Hiiragi, la segunda hija de la familia, acercándose peligrosamente al cuello de Shota mientras ambos se encuentran en una habitación iluminada por la luna. Por ahora, no se ha confirmado una fecha de estreno , aunque se sabe que UNLIMITED PRODUCE by TMS estará a cargo de la planificación y producción del proyecto. Tampoco se han revelado los integrantes del elenco de voces ni el equipo principal de animación. Una familia de vampiros con mucho amor para dar La historia sigue a Shota Minamoto, un estudiante de secundaria que vive en un hogar para niños después de quedarse huérfano. Su suerte parece cambiar cuando una familia adinerada decide adoptarlo y llevarlo a vivir a una enorme residencia de estilo japonés. Sus nuevos familiares lo reciben con los brazos abiertos, por lo que el muchacho comienza a sentirse cómodo en un lugar que finalmente puede llamar hogar. Sin embargo, la tranquilidad dura bastante poco. Una noche, Shota es atacado por alguien que intenta beber su sangre, descubriendo que todos los integrantes de su nueva familia son vampiros . Para empeorar las cosas, tendrá que compartir techo con tres hermosas hermanas que tampoco parecen tener demasiados problemas con su peculiar dieta. La gran pregunta es si realmente lo adoptaron para convertirlo en parte de la familia o si simplemente estaban buscando algo para cenar. La obra combina comedia romántica, convivencia familiar y elementos sobrenaturales, aunque con una atmósfera algo más oscura que otros trabajos de Yoshikawa. De hecho, la propia autora comentó que ha prestado especial atención al contraste entre los ambientes luminosos del día y las escenas nocturnas del manga, por lo que espera que la iluminación de la luna sea uno de los aspectos más llamativos de la adaptación animada. Cabe recordar que Hiragi-san's House of Vampires , conocido en Japón como Hiiragi-san no Kyuuketsu Jijou , comenzó como una historia autoconclusiva publicada en 2019. Posteriormente, el manga inició su serialización en la revista Bessatsu Shonen Magazine de Kodansha en octubre de 2021. La obra cuenta actualmente con seis volúmenes recopilatorios, mientras que el séptimo tiene previsto su lanzamiento para el próximo 16 de diciembre en Japón. Por el momento, los responsables no han compartido más detalles sobre la adaptación, así que habrá que esperar para conocer cuándo podremos ver las desventuras de Shota con su nueva familia. Mientras tanto, el manga también se encuentra disponible en inglés a través del servicio K Manga de Kodansha. ¿Te animarías a vivir con tres hermosas hermanas vampiro, o saldrías corriendo de la mansión en cuanto alguna comenzara a mirarte demasiado el cuello? title: Japanese government announces criteria for creating backup capital of Japan
summary: Four cities are the most likely candidates to become vice-capitals in case Tokyo is struck by an incapacitating natural disaster. Over the course of history, Japan has had several capital cities. Most famously, the imperial court was previously located in Kyoto, and before that in Nara. There was also a period of around 150 years […]
details: Four cities are the most likely candidates to become vice-capitals in case Tokyo is struck by an incapacitating natural disaster . Over the course of history, Japan has had several capital cities. Most famously, the imperial court was previously located in Kyoto, and before that in Nara. There was also a period of around 150 years when Kamakura, by nature of being the then-ruling shogunate’s base of power, operated as the de-facto capital. In 1868, though, the capital was moved to Edo, resulting in the entire city being renamed Tokyo, which literally means “eastern capital.” And while Tokyo isn’t in danger or losing that status, the Japanese government has now decided on a set of criteria for cities that want to become Japan’s official backup capital . The idea of designating a fukushuto (literally “vice-capital”) has been one that proponents have been kicking around for a while. Initially it was spearheaded by the Nippon Ishin (Japan Innovation) Party, a political group with a great deal of influence in Osaka , Japan’s third-largest city by population. The purposed purpose would be to have a backup plan in place in the event of a natural disaster in the Tokyo area, such as a large earthquake or eruption of Mt. Fuji, rendering government institutions in Tokyo unable to function. ▼ Osaka’s reputation for making superior takoyaki (octopus balls) compared to Tokyo, while not explicitly stated, was no doubt seen as an important factor as well. Seeking support from a potential coalition with Nippon Isshin voters, Japan’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party also began putting its weight behind the idea , and after agreeing to move forward with the initiative last summer , Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s cabinet has now released a set of criteria for cities applying for backup capital status. To qualify, the backup capital city must be located within a prefecture that contains at least 1.2 percent of Japan’s total population and accounts for at least 2.1 percent of the nation’s GDP . It must also be located sufficiently far enough from Tokyo to be outside the area of effect of any disaster that would incapacitate the current capital, and it must also have facilities for at least half of the 28 classifications of national government field offices . The distance-from-Tokyo requirement eliminates the city of Yokohama, since despite being Japan’s second-largest city, it’s only about 30 minutes south of the capital, so any natural disaster causing significant damage to one is likely to hit the other hard as well. However, despite Osaka politicians having been the ones who got the ball rolling on this whole vice-capital idea, they now seem to have rivals for that designation. In addition to Osaka, Aichi, Fukuoka, and Hokkaido also meet the cabinet’s criteria, and it is suggested that those prefectures’ legislators will make a push for the cities of Nagoya, Fukuoka, and Sapporo, respectively, to be chosen as a backup capital, though the current framework of the ordinance doesn’t explicitly prohibit multiple cities from being awarded the status . It’s worth noting that, according to the Japanese government’s National Personnel Authority, there are more than 40,000 government employees working in Tokyo’s Kasumigaseki district, where the majority of the city’s government facilities are located . While the vice-capital initiative doesn’t call for a complete 1:1 backup for every single office and worker, it would, as a matter of course, require some level of redundancy, and the related hiring and infrastructure development, funded by tax revenue, could represent a significant economic windfall for any city chosen as a vice-capital, and also give local legislators substantially more political clout. There’s also the question of whether debating and choosing backup capital cities is the most effective use of politicians’ time and energy, considering that rising costs of living, stagnating wages, and crime are probably more immediate concerns for the vast majority of ordinary citizens and residents of Japan. The cabinet is expected to spend the next year or so drafting the fundamental policies for how the vice-capital site would operate, which is slated to be presented next October prior to official site selections. title: Japan’s mini Shikoku Pilgrimage walking tour left us feeling immensely satisfied
summary: The full pilgrimage takes weeks to complete, but if you’ve got a couple hours, this Matsuyama experience will show you what makes the tradition so special. The Shikoku Pilgrimage route is, unquestionably, a great Japan travel experience. After all, people have been walking it, tracing the footsteps of famed Buddhist monk Kukai (also known as […]
details: The full pilgrimage takes weeks to complete, but if you’ve got a couple hours, this Matsuyama experience will show you what makes the tradition so special . The Shikoku Pilgrimage route is, unquestionably, a great Japan travel experience. After all, people have been walking it, tracing the footsteps of famed Buddhist monk Kukai (also known as Kobo Daishi), for 1,200 years now. However, the full route, which goes all around the island of Shikoku, is also a very time-consuming travel experience, taking roughly six weeks if you do it on foot. Odds are you don’t have that much time, and neither did we on our recent visit to the Shikoku city of Matsuyama in Ehime Prefecture . What we could fit into our itinerary, though, was a 90-minute Pilgrimage Experience Guided Walk which takes you to one of the 88 temples along the route, with guidance in traditional pilgrimage customs along the way. We and the other participants gathered at the pre-arranged meeting point on Matsuyama’s Dogo Shopping Street , not far from the city’s famous Dogo Onsen hot spring bathhouse. There we met our guide, who provided each of us with a sleeveless hakue , the white cloth tunic worn by Shikoku pilgrims, a sugegasa (conical straw hat), and kongozue (walking stick). ▼ There’s no mask that’s part of the outfit, that’s just a little privacy mark. As you might remember from the glowing review from our ace reporter Mr. Sato , Japanese straw hats are surprisingly comfortable, since not only do they keep the sun off of you, their construction means they don’t sit directly on top of your head like a baseball cap or other Western-style hats, providing better air circulation and to help keep you cool, all good things when you’re walking to and from temples. There’s a more morbid reason for the white tunics, though . The Shikoku Pilgrimage doesn’t present any grave dangers in the modern era, but centuries ago, when you couldn’t just whip out your phone and call for help if you became sick, injured, or lost, embarking on the route carried the risk that you might not make it back home. In Buddhist funeral rites, the body of the deceased is wrapped in a white garment prior to cremation, and the Shikoku pilgrimage tunic is white so that if someone were to meet with an untimely death along the way, they would already by properly dressed for cremation . But, to be clear, you won’t be on any mortal danger as part of this guided mini-pilgrimage, in which you walk from Dogo Onsen to Ishiteji Temple, the 51st of the 88 temples on the pilgrimage route . It takes about 20 minutes to reach the temple, and along the way we spotted such quant aspects of the neighborhood as haiku mailboxes in which anyone can submit a haiku poem they’ve written, from which a committee selects the best works every three months for awards. We also saw numerous ashiyu open-air foot baths filled with hot spring water, as well as a statue of Matsuyama-born master haiku poet Masaoka Shiki reflecting his other great passion, baseball. ▼ The guy was also pretty fond of sweet bean bread . As our group progressed further away from the bustling Dogo Shopping Street, we noticed local residents politely greeting us . “Good morning,” one would say, followed by another encouraging us with “Hang in there.” We asked our guide is these were friends or acquaintances acknowledging us by extension of their relationship with him, but he told us no, he’d never met these specific residents. With the pilgrimage route being such an important part of Shikoku culture, residents have made a custom of showing warmhearted respect to those walking the route, either in whole or part . We then reached Ishiteji Temple, where we learned another unique part of Shikoku culture. Soon after entering the temple grounds, we came to a stone bridge, and our guide instructed us to be careful not to tap our walking sticks on it as we crossed . This sort of specific prohibition isn’t the norm at temples in Japan, but as the guide explained, it’s connected to Kukai. When he was doing the very first Shikoku Pilgrimage back in the ninth century, Japan didn’t exactly have a robust leisure hotel industry. Sure, there were scattered inns here and there, but a lot of times Kukai didn’t have a roof over his head when he had to make camp for the night, and so he’d often sleep underneath bridges. Because of that, pilgrims should avoid hitting the upper surface of bridges with their walking sticks, as a metaphorical show of respect and consideration to the monk who might have been sleeping below . Ishiteji has two halls, where we lit candles and incense. Again, our guide gentle reminded us of the importance of consideration for others on the pilgrimage route, recommending that we place our lit offerings at the highest, farthest back, and most laterally centralized positions, so that those who came after us could place there’s without having to pass their hands over our flames. After that, we took a short rest and munched on some roasted mochi, a specialty of the temple that pilgrims have been enjoying for generations , and sipped a cup of green tea, which are offered as a set for 600 yen (US$3.80). As with a lot of temple visits and activities in Japan, the Pilgrimage Experience Guided Walk isn’t presented with an atmosphere of severe solemnity, nor as something only for individuals of markedly devout Buddhist faith, and can be participated in and enjoyed as a cultural experience rather than a strictly religious one. That said, there’s something special about knowing you’re helping keep a tradition alive more than a millennium after it started, and the kind greetings we received from townspeople along the way put us in a contemplative but happy mood that stayed with us long after we were back where we’d started in Dogo. title: Japan ends tax-free shopping system for foreign tourists, new refund request system now in effect
summary: What to be aware of as Japan tightens the rules for tourists saving 10 percent on their purchases. As of November 1, Japan has ended its tax-free shopping system for foreign tourists. Up until now, non-residents making purchases in Japan could avoid paying sales tax when shopping at participating stores by showing their passport as […]
details: What to be aware of as Japan tightens the rules for tourists saving 10 percent on their purchases . As of November 1, Japan has ended its tax-free shopping system for foreign tourists . Up until now, non-residents making purchases in Japan could avoid paying sales tax when shopping at participating stores by showing their passport as long as their total purchase price came to 5,000 yen (US$31.50) or more. As sales tax in Japan is generally 10 percent, and most major retailers, as well as a great many smaller ones, offered this service, overseas visitors to Japan were able to save a considerable amount of money, especially with shopping having become an especially popular activity for foreign tourists benefiting from the weak yen. The tax-free arrangement has now been replaced by a tax-refund system. Foreign tourists will now be required to pay sales tax in full at the time of purchase, and then apply for the amount to be refunded prior to their departure flight from Japan . Under the new system, travelers will still need to show their passport when purchasing items at retailers. Then, at the airport or seaport that you’re leaving Japan from, you’ll need to complete a tax refund application process at a kiosk or electronic self-service terminal . After showing your passport, the customs agent or terminal screen will inform you whether or not your application requires an additional inspection, and if it does, you’ll need to show all of the items that you’re seeking a tax refund for. In other words, you’ll need to complete the application process, and the inspection too, if required, before checking in your luggage. ▼ Self-service terminals will display either a green or red notice after you present your passport. Maps showing the locations of the terminals and inspection areas inside Japan’s major airports can be found online here . ▼ Terminal and inspection areas (marked in blue) inside Haneda Airport’s Terminal 2, International Flights Area (3rd floor) ▼ Haneda Airport Terminal 3 (3rd floor) In addition, travelers departing from Narita, Haneda, Kansai, Chubu Centrair International Airport, Fukuoka, New Chitose, and Naha airports can perform the application online through the Visit Japan Web website . However, doing so requires being connecting to a dedicated Wi‑Fi network for the procedure within the international departure lobby, so you’ll need to be at the airport either way. Once the procedure is complete, you can designate whether you wish to receive your refund via your credit card company or a bank transfer . The Japan Customs website does not mention a timeframe for refund processing, but a few weeks is likely, so you’ll want to make sure you’re not counting on that money for anything critical like rent or groceries. ▼ Narita International Airport Terminal 1 (4th floor) ▼ Narita International Airport Terminal 2 (3rd floor) So what prompted this change? Well, Japan’s sales tax is technically a “consumption tax,” and proponents of waiving it for foreign tourists figure that if the items aren’t going to be used/consumed in Japan, there’s no need to levy a tax on those purchases, which makes prices lower for tourists and helps boost sales for retailers. Japan’s tax-exemption system was basically operating on the honor system in that regard, though, which left the door open for dishonorable types to pass off or resell the tax-free items within the country. Changing to a tax refund system gives customs officials a way to confirm that the items really are going to be taken out of Japan before the purchasing tourist benefits from the untaxed price, and while not all travelers requesting a refund will be subject to inspection, it’s probavbly something you should be prepared for if you’ve done a lot of shopping during your trip. Something to be careful about regarding the tax refund system is that all items purchased at the same time (i.e. on the same receipt) are counted as a single, unbreakable unit . So, for example, if you purchase five items at the same time, and you get flagged for an inspection, you have to be able to present all five of those items to qualify for the tax refund for that purchase. If you’re missing even one, you won’t be eligible for a refund for the other four item, either. Likewise, if you purchase, say, multiple bottles of skincare lotion and opened one of them to use during your time in Japan, you won’t be able to claim a refund for the others unless they were purchased as a separate transaction/on a separate receipt. In addition, tax refund requests must be made within 90 days of an item’s purchase , though since 90 days is the standard tourist visa length for international visitors to Japan, this won’t be an issue for most shoppers. ▼ Narita International Airport Terminal 3 (2nd floor) Finally, under the new regulations it is the traveler’s responsibility to complete the procedure within time to check in for their flight. If you don’t, there’s no framework for requesting refunds at a later date, so if you stand to get a lot back, you’ll want to make sure to get to the airport early, though with the system being brand-new, there are not yet any official guidelines as to how long the procedure will take. title: This hot spring near Osaka’s Kansai Airport resolves the pick-two-out-of-three bathhouse dilemma
summary: Perfect for when you’ve got to fly, but want to soak. Generally, when it comes to hot springs in Japan, you can pick two of the following three things: convenient location, beautiful view, and not crowded. Someplace with a convenient location and nice scenery? Be prepared to share the tub with a whole lot of […]
details: Perfect for when you’ve got to fly, but want to soak . Generally, when it comes to hot springs in Japan, you can pick two of the following three things: convenient location, beautiful view, and not crowded. Someplace with a convenient location and nice scenery? Be prepared to share the tub with a whole lot of other people. Great view and small crowds? Probably going to have to be some small, hidden place way off the beaten path. Centrally located but not crowded? Odds are it’s because the ambiance isn’t that impressive. But it turns out sometimes you can have it all, like we did on our recent visit to Senshu no Yu . ▼ Natural Hot Spring Senshu no Yu (天然温泉 泉州の湯) Senshu is the old name for the Osaka region, and yes, Senshu no Yu is located within Osaka Prefecture. As a matter of fact, it’s located very close to Kansai International Airport , central Japan’s largest air travel hub. Kansai International is on an island that’s connected to the mainland by the Sky Gate Bride R, and as soon as you get across it, siting right there is Senshu no Yu . The bathhouse is about a 10-minute walk from Rinku Town Station on the Nankai Airport Line/JR Kansai Airport Line, which is itself only a six-minute ride from the airport, so this is a very convenient location is you’re looking to enjoy a hot spring bath as soon as possible after arriving in Japan, or maybe to indulge in one more right before you fly home . As for the view, it’s quite beautiful, with both the glass-in indoor and open-air baths giving you expansive lines of sight out across the bay. OK, so this place has to be packed, right? Let’s head on in from the first-floor entrance, up to the lobby on the second floor, and… …huh. It’s not like the interior is run-down or short on amenities, either. Everything was invitingly clean, from the tatami-floor relaxation space with shelves of manga to read to the cafe. If you want something more substantial to eat, there’s also a restaurant… …with a nice, chill vibe and more great views. OK…so is this place super pricey? Nope . Weekday admission is 900 yen (US$5.65), and on weekends and holidays they charge 1,000. If you didn’t bring your own towel, hand towels can be rented for 100 yen, and bath towels for 200. ▼ Entrance to the baths Senshu no Yu was even chosen among the country’s top 30 scenic-view hot springs by users of Japanese Internet portal Nifty. So what’s the catch? We’re not entirely sure, but it might have something to do with what most travelers think of when they hear “Osaka.” Osaka City is Japan’s third-largest city by population, and brings to mind the bustling streets of the Dotonbori canal district and its huge selection of shops and restaurants. Senshu no Yu, though located inside Osaka Prefecture, is in the town of Izumisano, which is way on the southern outskirts of Osaka City. Downtown Osaka is about an hour by train to the northeast of Senshu no Yu, and there’s not much in the way of sightseeing attractions in any other direction once you get across the bridge from the airport. The result is that most people just zoom right past the neighborhood without ever realizing why it’s worth making a special stop in. It should be noted that there is a hotel next door to Senshu no Yu, and with more and more travelers coming to Japan, it might not have its hidden-in-plain-view status for long. For now, though, it’s a rare chance to enjoy a hot spring soak without having to compromise on convenience, ambiance, or crowdedness. title: Starbucks Japan invites us to par-tea with its new Earl Gray Frappuccino [Taste test]
summary: Three new drinks, featuring seven kinds of tea, join the Starbucks Japan menu. This year’s Halloween parties are over and done with, but that doesn’t mean the fun is over for sweets fans. On November 2, Starbucks Japan rolled out no fewer than three new sweetly soothing beverages, and we rushed out to try them […]
details: Three new drinks, featuring seven kinds of tea, join the Starbucks Japan menu . This year’s Halloween parties are over and done with, but that doesn’t mean the fun is over for sweets fans. On November 2, Starbucks Japan rolled out no fewer than three new sweetly soothing beverages , and we rushed out to try them all. “Let’s par-tea” is the theme of this new lineup which aims to please lovers of puns and black tea, and while all three of them looked very tempting, we felt the strongest allure from Starbucks Japan’s newest Frappuccino, the Earl Grey Chocolate Frappuccino . By pouring a bunch of chocolate chips into an Earl Grey tea base , Starbucks has created something that appeals to a sophisticated sweet tooth, especially with the partnering presences of chocolate sauce and a swirl of whipped cream on top. And since Japan starts getting into the Christmas mood right after Halloween, you can dress up your 690-yen (US$4.30) Earl Grey Chocolate Frappuccino with a Christmas cookie for an additional 70 yen. The bright-colored Christmas present-shaped confectionary made for a cheery visual accent against the dark color of the Frappuccino itself, and while the combination looked so pretty we almost felt bad about drinking it, that hesitation only lasted until the moment it fired up our taste receptors. Our resident Frappuccino expert K. Masami handled taste-testing duties, and says that the elegantly aromatic sensation of Earl Grey tea arrives first, creating a serenely relaxing mood . The sweetness of the chocolate chips come next, but it blends smoothly with the tea notes while adding in some crunchy texture. As you continue to sip, or swirl your straw around, more of the chocolate sauce gets drawn into the mix, upping the sweetness but without becoming unpleasantly cloying, especially with the whipped cream helping to smooth together the various component flavors . Up next: the Joyful Medley Strawberry Creamy Tea Latte . This 650-yen latte features Starbucks Joyful Medley holiday tea mixture of black tea, oolong tea, and jasmine tea, plus a touch of apricot flavor . Beloved by fans for its complex taste that nonetheless comes to a clean finish, the Joyful Medley is joined for this drink by fresh cream, strawberry mouse, and a sprinkling of freeze-dried strawberry bits across the top . Our Joyful Medley Strawberry Creamy Tea Latte was also joined by the optional cookie topping, and this time we got a Christmas tree (there’s also a possible Santa hat cookie, adding a bit of a gacha element). Once again, this is a beautiful drink to look at, but tastes too good to spend very much time only visually admiring. The comforting blend of teas, rich creaminess, and sweetly tart strawberry flavors were so good together that Masami almost stopped sipping to give the drink a round of gleeful applause, and she especially recommends it to Starbucks fans who look forward to the Joyful Medley blend every year as a fresh new way to enjoy the blend. And finally, Masami checked out Starbucks Japan’s new Royal Milk Tea (620 yen). An original blend of Darjeeling, Assam and Ceylon tea , this one might not be as inventive as the other drinks we taste-tested here, but it’s still very satisfying, especially in your order your hot on a chilly autumn evening. All three drinks are listed as limited-time items, and since Starbucks Japan tends to get very busy with rapidly releasing new items as we get closer to the end of the year, it’s probably best to have your tea par-tea as soon as you can. title: Tokyo Skytree set to offer breathtaking Diamond Fuji natural phenomenon view this month
summary: The Tokyo landmark is a perfect spot on an ancient ley line of spiritual power to view the sight of Mt. Fuji with a diamond of light on its summit. Twice per year around February and November, anyone close enough to see Mt. Fuji can witness Diamond Fuji, a natural phenomenon when the rising or […]
details: The Tokyo landmark is a perfect spot on an ancient ley line of spiritual power to view the sight of Mt. Fuji with a diamond of light on its summit . Twice per year around February and November, anyone close enough to see Mt. Fuji can witness Diamond Fuji , a natural phenomenon when the rising or setting sun aligns perfectly with the mountain’s peak. When the conditions are just right, the sun’s rays then pan outward, giving the appearance of a shining diamond ring nestled on top of Japan’s highest mountain. This stunning phenomenon is next predicted to happen on November 8 around 4:30 p.m. ▼ The view of Diamond Fuji in November 2025 While any relatively tall spot in the Greater Tokyo Area is prime viewing to catch a glimpse of Diamond Fuji, the Tokyo Skytree ‘s two main viewing platforms–the Observation Deck at 350 meters (1,1448 feet) high and the Observation Galleria at 450 meters high–have a special claim to fame as to why Diamond Fuji is best viewed from one of them. ▼ Crowds gathered at the Tokyo Skytree Observation Deck at the Diamond Fuji phenomenon in February 2026 As described on the Tokyo Skytree’s website, the landmark was actually constructed on a kind of spiritual pathway that links several significant sites in the Kanto region: “Tokyo Skytree is built on a ‘ley line,’ a straight line connecting ancient ruins and sacred sites such as Mt. Fuji, Meiji Jingu Shrine, the Imperial Palace (formerly Edo Castle), and Kashima Jingu Shrine (Kashima City, Ibaraki Prefecture), and is said to be a place where positive energy gathers.” Therefore, by viewing Diamond Fuji from a location on this line, tradition says that you can essentially charge yourself with plenty of positive energy for the months to come–similar to visiting one of Japan’s various “ power spots .” ▼ Highlighted locations from left to right: Mt. Fuji, Meiji Shrine, Imperial Palace, Tokyo Skytree, and Kashima Shrine Regular Tokyo Skytree entrance fees apply for viewing the Diamond Fuji phenomenon on November 8. Viewing conditions are also unpredictable depending on the weather conditions, so please be prepared in advance. In the case of stormy weather, you may want to check out these picks for the top ten indoors attractions in Japan and Tokyo specifically instead. title: Shoplifting prevention guard arrested for shoplifting boot from store he was guarding

details: Those boots weren’t made for walking away with . In tough economic times, where even stores are switching to automated checkouts to save money, it’s no surprise that incidents of shoplifting have been steadily rising in Japan. To combat this, some retailers have employed what are known as “manbiki G-men,” plainclothes security guards whose role is to patrol stores and prevent sticky-fingered shoppers . Although the name is a throwback to prohibition-era FBI agents in the USA, these guards have no government authority like the police. Instead, they keep an eye on shoppers, shadow anyone suspected of shoplifting until they leave the store without paying, and then make a citizen’s arrest. But having manbiki G-men watch shoppers begs the question of who is watching the manbiki G-men. The answer to that question has revealed itself recently at a home improvement store in Hiroshima Prefecture on 27 October. ▼ The incident occurred at the Home Plaza Nafco in the picturesque town of Sera. At about 11 a.m. on that morning, a plainclothes police officer spotted the plainclothes security guard taking a single rubber boot, concealing it in his clothing, and attempting to take it from the store without paying . It was later revealed that the man is actually employed by the same store as a manbiki G-man, but it is unclear if he was on duty at the time of the incident. About a month prior to this, the store had contacted police about an uptick in shoplifting there, which put them on high alert. After being arrested on-site by the plainclothes police officer, the 66-year-old suspect admitted to the crime, saying he stole the single boot because he needed it . Though with a tragically ironic twist, it was an open-and-shut case. Once again, a man’s desire for a single rubber boot corrupted him to the point of abusing the power entrusted to him by his employer. “It’s always darkest right under the lighthouse.” “I guess they need some manbiki G-men G-men.” “Maybe he was just trying to get inside the head of his target.” “Are they not even paying their G-men enough to get some rubber boots?” “We’re not going to make it, are we? The country, I mean.” “You either die a G-man or live long enough to become a shoplifter.” “Fascinating! It’s like the end of a Poirot story.” “I wonder if he just needed one boot or was planning to make two trips.” Regardless of whether or not he really did need a second piece of footwear, we can be certain the home improvement store will be figuratively giving him the boot. Hopefully, he was just caught up in the thrill and excitement of stealing some Wellies, because that’s at least slightly less bleak than an employed person being unable to afford a pair on his own. So, let that be a lesson to all you junior G-men out there. While bustin’ two-bit flimflammers, it can be right tempting to get yer mitts on some cabbage for yourself too, but the only easy street that lands you on leads straight to the hoosegow. details: Fender celebrates Red and Green’s 30th anniversary with guitars saluting the Pokémon world in both looks and sound . In the English-speaking world, the start of the Pokémon video game series were the paired releases of Pokémon Red and Blue for the Game Boy in 1998. However, unbeknownst to many young fans at the time, the real origins of the franchise had come out in Japan two years prior, and were titled Pokémon Red and Green . Here in 2026, the global Poké-fan community has a more comprehensive picture of the franchise’s history, which brings us to the appropriate color schemes for the latest collaboration celebrating Pokémon’s 30th anniversary, a pair of customized guitars created in partnership with Fender Japan . In a parallel to how mainline Pokémon games customarily have a similar but still different sibling, so too has Fender chosen two different models of guitar for this team-up, the Made in Japan Pokémon “Red Version” Stratocaster and Made in Japan Pokémon “Green Version” Telecaster . Within the series’ visual design language, the color red is often associated with Fire-type Pocket Monsters, and green with Grass-types, so the body of each guitar is covered in pixel art of species from those categories . More fan-service flair can be found on the neck, where Poké Balls are subtly scattered about… …and the backside features a Pokémon 30th anniversary plate . In addition to their visual salutes to the Pokémon world, these made-in-Japan guitars make an audio one too . Push in the volume knob, and you can activate what Fender has dubbed the instruments’ “8-Bit Sound System Mode,” a clever audio effect that gives the guitar’s sound a quality reminiscent of nostalgic chiptunes, which should lend itself really well to playing covers of classic Pokémon games’ soundtracks. ▼ A demonstration video of the 8-Bit Sound System Mode 楽器メーカーFender®とコラボした『ポケットモンスター 赤・緑』デザインのギターが、ポケモンセンターオンラインに登場！ 11月19日（木）、12時から抽選販売の応募が開始されるよ。 音色に8-bitサウンドが加わるギミックも搭載！ ぜひ動画で聴いてみてね。 https://t.co/c6Xlr0hX3H #ポケモンセンター pic.twitter.com/ydajspcaQ0 — ポケモン公式 (@Pokemon_cojp) October 30, 2026 Each guitar also comes bundled with a selection of pixel art picks, plus a custom hardcase and certificate of authenticity . Because they’ll be available in limited quantities, both guitars, priced at 396,000 yen (US$2,490) each, will be offered for sale through a lottery system from the Pokémon Center Online store, which will be accepting applications between noon on November 19 and 4:59 p.m. on November 24 (Japan time). title: Beautiful Ghibli diorama kits lets you build anime characters’ homes inside yours [Photos]
summary: Papercraft models are small in size, but colossally cool for fans of Studio Ghibli. Earlier in the year Ghibli Park added a new exhibit consisting of over 30 large dioramas made by famed anime director Hayao Miyazaki. Odds are, though, that you don’t have that much space to devote to your love of Ghibli’s art […]
details: Papercraft models are small in size, but colossally cool for fans of Studio Ghibli . Earlier in the year Ghibli Park added a new exhibit consisting of over 30 large dioramas made by famed anime director Hayao Miyazaki . Odds are, though, that you don’t have that much space to devote to your love of Ghibli’s art and environments, but Japanese papercraft company Sankei does have a way to let you bring a little piece of the Ghibli world into your home. Going on sale November 3 are three new entries in Sankei’s Miniatuart Mini Plus line, recreating locations from Howl’s Moving Castle, Kiki’s Delivery Service, and Arrietty . Each of them starts as a box filled with sheets of paper from which to build the walls and interior, and after you assemble everything the box then becomes a stand for the completed diorama. Though the scale is compact and the building materials simple, the kits contain an incredible level of charming detail. Howl’s hearth , for example, is cluttered with all sorts of magical baubles and reference materials, just as you’d expect the eccentric wizard’s living quarters to be, and even fire spirit Calcifer makes an appearance. The room that Kiki and Jiji rent from bakery owner Osono is decidedly less chaotic, but still has a lived-in feel with the witch’s laundry hanging up to dry, her broom leaning against the windowsill, and Jiji making sure not to leave any dirty pawprints on the nice clean floor. The Kiki’s kit also has the most detailed exterior, which really helps create the atmosphere of it being a miniaturized loft that scaled-down version of the characters could live inside. ▼ The kits’ boxes/bases bear different illustrations on different sides, too, giving you one more reason to view them from different angles Rounding out the trio is Arietty’s family’s living room . This one comes with an extra dash of coolness because the scale of the diorama (6 centimeters [2.4 inches] square) works as a reminder that Arietty and her kin are all so tiny that most of the humans whose house they lived inside of never noticed them. All of the locations are filled with cozy vibes, but they are listed on Sankei’s website as being advanced-difficulty kits, with an estimated time of five hours or more to build Kiki’s room, and 10 hours or more for the others. Kiki’s kit is also the lowest-priced of the bunch at 4,290 yen (US$27), followed by Arrietty’s (6,160 yen) and Howl’s (6,600 yen). All three can be ordered starting November 3 through Sankei’s Rakuten online storefront ( here , here , and here ). title: This semi-secret, totally free footbath in downtown Tokyo is completely awesome
summary: The Museum of Narratives has an oasis for your feet. They say there’s no such thing as a free lunch, but it turns out there is a free foot bath in Tokyo. It’s not some rinky-dink little tub in some obscure spot on the outskirts of the capital, either, but right in the middle of […]
details: The Museum of Narratives has an oasis for your feet . They say there’s no such thing as a free lunch, but it turns out there is a free foot bath in Tokyo . It’s not some rinky-dink little tub in some obscure spot on the outskirts of the capital, either, but right in the middle of downtown, near Takanawa Gateway Station on the Yamanote train line that encircles the city center. Takanawa Gateway is the newest station on the line, and is connected to a shopping, entertainment, and cultural development called Takanawa Gateway City , part of which is MoN Takanawa: The Museum of Narratives . The museum, which opened in March, hosts rotating artistic and cultural events, but on our visit, we didn’t need to purchase a ticket, because we weren’t heading inside the main exhibition areas. Instead, our destination was someplace on the sixth-floor, an exterior area that many people aren’t aware of called the Ashiyu Terrace . Ashiyu is the Japanese word for “footbath,” and that’s exactly what you’ll find here! This outdoor urban oasis has an outer ring of greenery, and beyond that offers impressively open views of the surrounding cityscape, of a kind that’s not easy to come by this deep in downtown without going to a skyscraper’s upper floors. This is thanks to the terrace’s position adjacent to the train tracks, plus Takanawa Gateway’s proximity to the next station to the south, Shinagawa. Shinagawa is one of Japan’s densest rail hubs, and the seven different lines that converge there each need their own amount of space as they approach the station, creating a rare broad, low patch in downtown Tokyo’s urban topography that creates wide lines of sight. ▼ This also makes the MoN Takanawa footbath a great place for trainspotting rail fans. Because the foot bath is open-air, it’s probably not the most pleasant place to spend a blisteringly hot summer day or a frigidly cold winter evening. Right now, though, on a fall afternoon, the weather is perfect for this sort of thing, especially since in addition to a cozy-warm hot water area… …the Ashiyu Terrace also has a cold water area . This means you can start off in the warm section until you’re feeling nice and toasty, and once you get a little too hot, you can mosey on over to the other end of the bath and cool down. Then, if you’re anything like us, you’ll eventually migrate back to the warm section, and repeat the process a couple more times before you’re ready to leave this ankle-deep aquatic paradise. If you’re looking for more ways to enjoy traditional Japanese culture on the free-to-access museum grounds, there’s a little Shinto shrine on the rooftop… …and a tatami reed-floor relaxation room on the fourth floor with digital art displays, which is also free to access. ▼ The tatami mats are new enough that they still have a very noticeable relaxing earthy fragrance. Really, the only possibly negative thing we could say about the Ashiyu Terrace is that no towels are provided, but we’re happy to bring our own handkerchief to dry off with when the rest of this experience is this awesome. title: Japan’s TeamLab digital art group is opening a permanent museum in America
summary: Internationally acclaimed art collective will have a new home not far from Disneyland. Japan’s TeamLab has risen from relative obscurity to become one of the most admired digital art collectives in the world, using their technological wizardry and ethereally emotional sensibilities to craft experiences unlike those from anyone else. Their exhibits and museums regularly top […]
details: Internationally acclaimed art collective will have a new home not far from Disneyland . Japan’s TeamLab has risen from relative obscurity to become one of the most admired digital art collectives in the world, using their technological wizardry and ethereally emotional sensibilities to craft experiences unlike those from anyone else. Their exhibits and museums regularly top lists of must-visit places for artistically inclined travelers in Japan, but now it’s time for TeamLab itself to embark on an overseas journey, as it’s announced that it will be opening its very first permanent museum in the U.S. Sunny southern California is where TeamLab will be setting up in the States. The group’s facility will be part of the city of Anaheim’s currently in-development OCVIBE cultural, entertainment, and sports complex, which will also have green spaces, offices, hotels, and apartments. ▼ Examples of the sort of art that TeamLab creates TeamLab Museum Anaheim is the tentative name of the facility, but it won’t be a shock if they eventually decide on something with a little more pizazz, seeing as how their museums in Japan have creative names such as TeamLab Borderless or TeamLab Planets . The Anaheim museum is planned to have a total floor space of roughly 10,000 square meters (approximately 110,000 square feet). ▼ A preview image showing TeamLab Museum Anaheim, with its shimmery sea green exterior, connected by a pedestrian bridge to the Anaheim Regional Transportation Intermodal Center rail station, with Angel Stadium behind it on the opposite side of the 57 Freeway In announcing the Anaheim museum, TeamLab co-founder and director Toshiyuki Inoko said: “I am filled with happiness that we will be opening TeamLab’s first large-scale museum in America at OCVIBE in Anaheim. Through art, TeamLab seeks to explore the nature of consciousness and existence. Our exhibits change through the existence of people, with visitors themselves becoming part of the piece. By becoming immersed in the artwork, visitors are connected, without boundaries, to both the installation and the world. By gathering and placing ourselves alongside others in this location where sports, music, and culture intersect, we will come to perceive the world in new ways and share those perceptions with others.” OCVIBE is planned to open in phases, with the first coming in the spring of next year and featuring an amphitheater, restaurants, and park. TeamLab’s museum, though, is projected to open in 2030, but fans will tell you that the group’s creations are worth the wait, and that’s still two years earlier than the projected opening of its new Tokyo museum . title: Can Japan’s Self-Defense Forces legally open fire on a zombie horde?
summary: This legal discussion contains scenes of explicit violence and gore. It’s Halloween again, and what better way to ring in the spookiest of holidays than with some thought exercises on complex constitutional law issues. Although most zombie stories focus on a ragtag group of civilians coping with civilization collapsing all around them, the beginning of […]
details: This legal discussion contains scenes of explicit violence and gore . It’s Halloween again, and what better way to ring in the spookiest of holidays than with some thought exercises on complex constitutional law issues . Although most zombie stories focus on a ragtag group of civilians coping with civilization collapsing all around them, the beginning of the outbreak usually shows the military going all out in trying to eliminate the undead threat. And with many of these movies and TV shows taking place in the USA, it’s no surprise to see the armed forces meeting the waves of zombies with guns blazing. In Japan, however, such a response is not so simple. While most countries’ militaries operate on a principle of “anything shy of a war crime is fair game,” Japan’s Self-Defense Forces operate in the opposite way and require very strict conditions before they can perform a certain action . A good crash course in this can be found in our analysis on how the military can legally deal with a kaiju attack . Long story short, it is possible if Godzilla is classified as a “natural disaster” and the weapons used against him are classified as “tools” to neutralize the threat to Japan. Zombies are much more complicated, however. Although certain aspects of the Godzilla scenario can be applied here, the fact that the threat is or was human introduces bigger legal hurdles for military and police forces. A video recently posted in the Legal Insight series by Tonari no Bengoshi Hosokyoku looks at this situation in-depth, but while their legal knowledge is spot-on, I’m concerned with some of their zombie awareness. To start, much like with Godzilla, the SDF can be dispatched in a disaster relief capacity without issue. This means they can organize evacuations, set up barricades for shelters, and act in cases of self-defense to protect the public, just like police do. However, in this capacity, they cannot launch an assault on the zombies. One exception would be if the zombies were unleashed on Japan by a foreign government. This is the same reason that Godzilla cannot be considered an enemy combatant but King Ghidorah (sent by those jerks on Planet X) can. So, let’s say our zombies are homegrown from some virus or mushrooms or something. Now, the question is whether they are people or not . According to Legal Insight, if they are classified as living people, then killing them can be considered murder, but even if they’re dead, filling them full of lead is also the crime of desecrating human remains. However, Legal Insight also says that a zombie would be legally declared a corpse, and thus considered an “object” rather than a “person.” In this case, they could be treated in a way similar to wild animals that pose a threat to human life and be dealt with by the Self-Defense Forces using their guns as “tools,” much like with Godzilla. The desecration of a corpse charges would be outweighed by the need to protect lives, much like how scuttling an abandoned ship adrift in the ocean is deemed necessary despite the destruction of property involved. But I think that’s where they got it wrong. Despite all of our advances, humans are still not great at determining if something is alive or not. For legal purposes, however, Japan employs the “three signs of death” (shi no sanchoko) used by medical professionals: cardiac arrest, respiratory arrest, and loss of brainstem reflexes . If all three of these conditions are present at the same time and irreversible, then that person is deemed deceased. Legal Insight says that zombies do exhibit the three signs of death, but I beg to differ. This is a problematic claim because there have been so many different zombie stories with zombies of wildly varying abilities, but even despite that, I don’t think any of them even exhibits one of the three signs of death, let alone all three. Starting with cardiac arrest, zombies bleed when shot and clearly have muscle function, either of which would be impossible a beating heart. ▼ Your Honor, if it pleases the court, I’d like to submit this gnarly video of Claire doming a couple zombies in Resident Evil 2 Remake. As you can clearly see from the blood spurting from their neckholes, they demonstrate arterial pressure which can only be achieved by a functioning heart. And while they may not require it to function, zombies clearly breathe. How else do they make those “gnnnhhhurghhhh” noises? And brainstem reflexes? Baby, zombies are all about brainstem reflex. ▼ I’d now like to call Dr. Edwin Jenner of the CDC in the USA to the stand. He’ll explain to us that zombies have functioning brainstems beyond a shadow of a doubt. So, whether it’s the ambling Night of the Living Dead zombies or your parkour-running 28 Days Later zombies, they are legally living humans and, as such, it could be argued that zombies would have rights in Japan. This means a cop or soldier cannot open fire on a zombie simply because they gave them a dirty look or even if they start walking towards them menacingly. The violence used against them must be in direct proportion to their own unlawful attack… which I guess means all soldiers can do is bite the zombies back. So, in conclusion, the JSDF would be prohibited from gunning down zombies wholesale, and Japanese police would be legally obliged to arrest you for assault if one falls off the hood of your car while you drive away in a panic. That being said, in most zombie outbreaks the government seems to go down pretty quickly, and all laws just go out the window anyway. Happy Halloween! title: Guile cosplay goes with everyone for Halloween at SoraNews24 HQ [Photos]
summary: Go home and be a family man? Nah, we have to go to work. We keep SoraNews24 HQ clean enough so that we don’t have flies on the wall, but if you were to be, for instance, a shapeshifting tanuki disguised as a fern in the corner of our office on Friday, you might have […]
details: Go home and be a family man? Nah, we have to go to work . We keep SoraNews24 HQ clean enough so that we don’t have flies on the wall, but if you were to be, for instance, a shapeshifting tanuki disguised as a fern in the corner of our office on Friday, you might have heard the following conversation take place. Mr. Sato : “ Hey, you guys bring your Guile gear? ” P.K. : “ Yeah. ” Mr. Sato : “ OK. So, we doing this? ” Ahiruneko : “ We sure are. But, like, I really didn’t have much to bring. ” Mr. Sato : “ But, like, -how- are we supposed to do this? We just, like, become Guile? ” Seiji Nakazawa : “ Sure. No need to overthink it, right? ” P.K. : “ We all just turn into Guile, just like that? ” See, we have a tradition here at SoraNews24, where everyone who’s in the office on the day closest to Halloween dresses up in costume . We try to have some sort of theme, like dressing up as the trendiest desert drink of the year or trying to transform into actual parts of the Tokyo cityscape . This year, we settled on the theme of developer Capcom’s hit fighting video game series, Street Fighter, and since every release since Street Fighter II: Championship Edition has allowed players to pick the same character as each other, we decided that everyone in the office would become Guile . Mr. Sato : “ I think everybody already has their outfit sorted, so we better get started on our making our Guile hair. ” Takeshi Harada : “ How are we supposed to do that? ” Mr. Sato : “ All you need is some yellow paper, and some imagination. ” With Hollywood’s newest live-action Street Fighter adaptation currently playing in theaters, some might be tempted to accuse us of trying to piggyback on the movie’s hype train, but our Guile-loving credentials have been an established matter of public record for some time , as we previously published a literally hard-hitting investigative piece on the real-world effectiveness of Guile’s iconically cool-looking low-guard pose from the games. Takeshi : “ Am I doing it right? ” Mr. Sato : “ Hey, man, you gotta trust your own judgement when making Guile hair. ” Then, after 20 minutes of cutting, taping, and changing clothes in a wide-open office with no locker room… Mr. Sato: “OK, everybody set? Show us your Guiles!” So, uh, as you can see, even though everyone was dressed as the same character, there was still plenty of, let’s call them individual creative differences present in the final results. Let’s take a closer look at what everyone came up with. ▼ Seiji Guile! ▼ Yuichiro Guile! ▼ Ahiruneko Guile! ▼ Takeshi Guile! ▼ P.K. Guile! ▼ Yoshio Guile! ▼ Sato Guile! ▼ Go Hatori Guile, who actually wasn’t in the office this day but who joined the battle via a photo taken ahead of time! So who’s Guile was the best Guile? We left that judgement up to Seiji, since we felt like we kind of owed him one for all the physical punishment he took in that Guile blocking test. Seiji Guile : “ All right, you maggots! Line up for inspection! ” Seiji Guile : “ Sato Guile! You are the sorriest display of a Guile in this whole company! ” Sato Guile : “ What? But I thought I did pretty good. I even worked out extra to tone up my arms and shoulders for this. ” Seiji Guile : “ I didn’t expect anything more of you than using paper for your hair, but why did you put the crease in the front? That’s inexcusable! You’re a disgrace to our proud Guile traditions! ” Seiji Guile : “ Next! Yoshio Guile! You’re all right. I can tell you’re taking the mission seriously. ” Seiji Guile : “ Unlike the rest of these knuckleheads who just used drawing paper, you reinforced your spikes with construction paper. That’s the kind of ingenuity that we need to be ready to display in the field. ” Yoshio Guile : “ Sir! Thank you, sir! ” Seiji Guile : “ Next! Ahiruneko Guile! What in the name of a redizzy combo do you call this? ” Ahiruneko Guile : “ No good? ” Seiji Guile : “ No good at all! That sloppy, loose tank top is totally outside uniform regulations! ” Ahiruneko Guile : “ Well, I mean, I just bought it on Amazon, so it wasn’t like I could try it on and check the fit or anything… ” Seiji Guile : “ You think Guile would be caught dead in something like that? You’re a disgrace to the uniform! ” Seiji Guile : “ Next! P.K. Guile! ” P.K. Guile : “ Look, I’ll just get it out of the way and apologize right now. ” Seiji Guile : “ Well, at least you’ve got a scrap of self awareness. You know your pants are wrong, right? ” P.K. Guile : “ When I went to the thrift shop, this was all they had for camo pants. I know the color is wrong. ” Seiji Guile : “ No, actually Guile has alternate color versions with blue pants, so that’s not the problem. But what no one has ever seen is Guile rolling up his pants! ” Seiji Guile : “ Next! Takeshi Guile! ” Seiji Guile : “ You clearly didn’t understand the assignment either! A digital camouflage pattern? Seriously? You know Guile doesn’t wear that! ” Takeshi Guile : “ I went to a thrift store too, and this was the only pair of camo pants I could find. ” Seiji Guile : “ You’re endangering the whole mission by relying on thrift stores! Next time shop online if you need to and make sure you get the pattern right! ” Seiji Guile : “ Next! Yuichiro Guile! Let’s wrap this up! ” Seiji Guile : “ So tell me how you managed to forget you’re supposed to be Guile? You look like you just came from the kitchen or the beach! ” Seiji Guile : “ That hairline’s crammed all the way down onto your eyebrows, like you’re wearing chef’s hat! And shorts? Shorts?!! How’re you gonna have a proper street fight without proper pants? ” Seiji Guile : “ Aside from Yoshio and Go, none of you are ready to be Guile! Guess it’s up to me to whip you all into shape. ” Guiles : “ Yes, sir! ” Seiji Guile : “ ATTEN-TION! Company, form up and…flash kick charge pose! ” Guiles : “ Yes, sir! ” Seiji Guile : “ Crouching guard! ” Guiles : “ Yes, sir! ” Seiji Guile : “ Just you wait and see! I’ll turn you all into real Guiles yet! ” A Happy Hallo

title: Cold Stone is closing its final branch in all of east Japan, but it’s going down singing
summary: Parting is such very, very sweet sorrow. No one’s really watching their calories on October 31, right?
