details: Parting is such very, very sweet sorrow . No one’s really watching their calories on October 31 , right? Between trick-or-treating, Halloween parties, and all those tempting candy displays in the stores, there’s no better occasion for indulging your sweet tooth multiple times during the same day. And if you’re already leaving room for desserts, this Halloween is a very good time to make a visit to Cold Stone, because on October 31 they’re permanently closing their last remaining branch in east Japan . Cold Stone’s time in Japan has been a rollercoaster ride. The chain first showed up in Japan in 2005 and became an immediate sensation among sweets fans, with long lines forming to try the offerings of the American “creamery” and listening to the staff’s cheerful singing voices while they waited. For a while there, Cold Stone looked poised to enter the ranks of Japan’s lovingly adopted brands from the U.S. such as McDonald’s and Starbuck’s. Unfortunately, not long after Cold Stone Japan’s expansion plans heated up, consumer enthusiasm for the chain started to cool off. In time, branches started closing down, with the even vacating Tokyo entirely for a while. Eventually, though, Cold Stone found its way back to the capital. In 2023, it opened a new branch Tokyo’s Tama district, and then another in downtown’s trendy Harajuku neighborhood . ▼ The Harajuku branch, shortly after its opening in June of 2023 Sadly, neither of those comeback bids panned out, and by April of 2025, there were once again no Cold Stone branches anywhere in Tokyo, and the only remaining location in all of east Japan was located inside an outlet shopping mall in Tochigi Prefecture…which closed down one month later . But then this past summer came a ray of hope for Cold Stone fans in east Japan with the opening of a Cold Stone branch in the town of Kamakura in Kanagawa Prefecture , Tokyo’s neighbor to the south. Kamakura is a major sightseeing destination, with temples, shrines, hiking trails, and beaches, and it’s only about an hour by train from Tokyo, making it an easy daytrip for Tokyoites and travelers staying at hotels in the capital. ▼ Video of the Kamakura Cold Stone’s opening day on July 30 View this post on Instagram Being a big Cold Stone fan, our ace reporter Mr. Sato was thrilled to have the chain back in east Japan, and was looking forward to getting a scoop or two the next time he was down in Kamakura. The urgency on his plans to visit the city got rapidly cranked up, though, when on October 29 Cold Stone Japan announced through its official Instagram account that it would be permanently closing its Kamakura branch, and doing so in just two days’ time, on October 31 . So Mr. Sato dropped everything, dashed to the station, and rode the train to Kamakura. The Kamakura Cold Stone has a pretty good location. It’s outside JR Kamakura Station’s west exit, which isn’t as busy and developed as the east side of the structure, but there’s still a decent amount of foot traffic, especially since the shop is close to the transfer gates for the Enoden rail line that runs along the shore and provides ironically picturesque views. At this point, Mr. Sato might still have been able to delude himself into believing that there’d been some kind of mistake in Cold Stone’s Instagram announcement, and that the store wasn’t actually shutting down after just three months in business. But sure enough, there was a written notice posted at the counter that said: Cold Stone Creamery Kamakura Station Notice of closure We are grateful to the support shown by so many visitors since our opening. As of October 31, Cold Stone Creamery Kamakura Station will be closing. We wish to take this opportunity to sincerely thank all of our customers. We will continue to do our best to provide all of you with Happy Creamery experiences. We look forward to seeing all of your smiles again someday. Thank you so much for everything. So this was really going to be goodbye. Carefully weighing his options for this final Cold Stone session, Mr. Sato asked for Dobai chocolate ice cream in a chocolate waffle bowl, covered with chocolate sauce. “Is it OK if we sing?” asked the staff, unwaveringly cheerful, even now, and Mr. Sato said “Yes! Please!” “I was sad to hear you’ll be closing.” Said Mr. Sato after the song was finished and they handed him his order. “Yes, we only found out about it two days ago,” said the clerk, revealing that they’d apparently been as surprised as Mr. Sato was at the turn of events. ▼ Mr. Sato’s ice cream. He does not fool around when it comes to grand finales of his favorite dessert places. Mr. Sato couldn’t help silently wondering why it had to end like this . It’s not like Japan doesn’t like ice cream. As a matter of fact, Japan loves ice cream. Baskin-Robbins has over 1,000 branches in Japan , including one on the other side of Kamakura Station. Aside from specialty shops, fast food chains and snack stands sell ice cream all year round, as do convenience stores and super markets. So why can’t Cold Stone seem to get a stronger foothold in the country? The company hasn’t made any official statement explaining its woes, but as we’ve discussed before , it might have something to do with the kind of ice cream that Cold Stone serves not matching up with how Japan would like it served . Ice cream fans in Japan are fine with casual settings or eating on the go for simple frozen treats, like a modest-sized scoop of Baskin-Robbins or personal-size serving of Häagen-Dazs. On the other end of the spectrum, leisurely savoring a large, decadent parfait at a cozy or fashionable cafe is considered a highlight-of-the-day-caliber experience. Cold Stone, though, doesn’t really fit into either of those two scenarios . details: Here there be dragons and bargains . Generally, people don’t go to malls to buy daily necessities like paper towels or detergent. Mall shopping is primarily for fun or special-occasion purposes, and to make the atmosphere even more fun and special, sometimes outlet malls in Japan have collaborations with popular video game franchises. Maybe they put up a Final Fantasy Christmas tree for the holiday season, or set out some Super Mario cardboard character standees . And then there’s what Mitsui Outlet Park Fukuoka Marinoa is planning to do for its team-up with the Monster Hunter franchise. Two different giant beasts from developer Capcom’s hit series are scheduled to becoming residents of the mall, and we do mean giant beasts, as these statues will be “life-size” versions of Fire Wyvern Rathalos, known as the King of the Skies, and Leviathan Lagiacrus, King of the Seas . Because Monster Hunter’s gameplay system allows for variances in individual specimen sizes, we can’t say for sur how large the statues of Rathalos and Lagiacrus will be, but the preview images promise that they’ll be of sufficient stature that low-level adventurers would be ill-advised to attempt to solo them. Since the Monster Hunter: World installment in the series, particularly bold monsters have been able to engage in turf wars with one another should they both covet the same section of the environment, and it looks like Mitsui Outlet Park Fukuoka Marinoa’s Rathalos and Lagiacrus might not be the best of friends, as effects such as dramatic sound, lighting, and mist will be used to simulate battles between the two . The outlet mall, located near Meinohama Station in Fukuoka City, is slated to open this coming April , so you’ve got a few months to sort out your travel plans/put together a Monster Hunter team before the creatures appear. title: Burger King Japan shuns Shibuya Halloween spirit, but keeps it alive everywhere else
summary: No tricks or treats is the plan at Shibuya Center-gai, but cool sweets will be waiting at every other branch. In a way, I suppose you could accuse Burger King Japan of having lost its Halloween spirit. The chain’s Shibuya Center-gai branch in downtown Tokyo, just a short walk from the world-famous Shibuya Scramble intersection, […]
details: No tricks or treats is the plan at Shibuya Center-gai, but cool sweets will be waiting at every other branch . In a way, I suppose you could accuse Burger King Japan of having lost its Halloween spirit. The chain’s Shibuya Center-gai branch in downtown Tokyo , just a short walk from the world-famous Shibuya Scramble intersection, announced on Thursday that it’ll be closed for the entirety of October 31 . The storefront’s shutter will be down with a large 臨時休業 (“temporarily closed”) written across it, and the Burger King logo will even have an X over it to quickly communicate the message “No burgers here on Halloween!” This has become something of an annual tradition at the Shibuya Center-gai Burger King, stemming from the neighborhood’s attempts to clean up its image at Halloween . Shibuya was one of the first places in Japan where people began gathering in large numbers to celebrate Halloween, and what started as good-natured fun eventually turned into alcohol-soaked street parties with instances of vandalism, theft, and violence marring the unsanctioned gatherings. In recent years the authorities have been cracking down with measures such as restricting alcohol sales and setting up gates and barricades to more tightly control the flow of people in and out of Shibuya on and around Halloween night, as well as public awareness campaigns reminding people that public drinking, littering, and other forms of inconsiderate or unruly behavior are not allowed. And while there’s no government mandate prohibiting Burger King from staying open on October 31, the restaurant’s management evidently feels the wisest choice is to close the place and take the day off so as not to contribute to overcrowding in Shibuya on Halloween. That doesn’t mean that Burger King Japan is opposed to Halloween fun in general, though. As a matter of fact, at the same time that the Shibuya Center-gai location is closed, every other Burger King in Japan will be actively celebrating by inviting people to come on in and trick-or-treat! On October 31, all non-Shibuya Center-gai Burger Kings will be giving out free soft serve ice cream to the first 30 visitors age 18 or younger who come up to the counter and say “trick or treat.” There doesn’t appear to be any requirement that they order anything else, either, so this really is following the classic Halloween custom of giving out sweets simply for the asking. They’re even sweetening the free-sweets deal by tossing in a sheet of Halloween stickers. ▼ The ice cream here appears to be haunted, but that’s still better than not having ice cream right? Note, though, that the trick-or-treat ice cream is only available between 2 p.m. and 6 p.m., which means no having it for breakfast, but since trick-or-treating isn’t a morning activity, even this is in keeping with the spirit of Halloween. title: Evangelion announces collaboration with Hard Rock Cafe
summary: Get in the Hard Rock crossover, Shinji! The Hard Rock Cafe currently has two branches in Tokyo, one in the Roppongi Neighborhood and one attached to Ueno Station, but what if the restaurant had a Tokyo-3 branch? And no, we don’t mean a third branch in Tokyo, but a branch inside Tokyo-3, the city that serves […]
details: Get in the Hard Rock crossover, Shinji! The Hard Rock Cafe currently has two branches in Tokyo, one in the Roppongi Neighborhood and one attached to Ueno Station, but what if the restaurant had a Tokyo-3 branch? And no, we don’t mean a third branch in Tokyo, but a branch inside Tokyo-3, the city that serves as the main setting of Evangelion . That’s the concept behind a new collaboration between the giant robot anime series and music-themed restaurant chain, which has led to a new collection of crossover merch. Evangelion Unit-01 is the star here, featured on T-shirts with its iconic green-and-purple color scheme and AT field hexagonal pattern applied to the Hard Rock Logo. Three different colors are on offer, with white available at the Roppongi, Ueno Kyoto, and Universal Citywalk Osaka Hard Rock Cafes. Gray shirts will be on the rack at Roppongi, Yokohama, Citywalk Osaka, and the Namba store, while those looking for black shirts will find them at Ueno, Yokohama, Kyoto, and Namba. Also part of the lineup is a sukajan/Yokosuka jacket , which seems like a very appropriate canvas for this sort of East-meets-West endeavor. Rounding out the fashion selection is the Eva/Hard Rock cap , and Unit-01 and the series’ core pilot roster will also be appearing on shot glasses, magnets, and pins . The magnet and shot glass, pictures above, will include the name of the city in which they were purchased, but the pins will be specific to each Hard Rock location. The pins are limited-quantity items, with only 500 of each design being made and carrying a price of 3,080 yen (US$19), which is also the price of the magnet. The shot glass, meanwhile, is 1,980 yen, the shirts 5,940 yen, and the Yokosuka jacket, as is often the case for the embroidered garments, is a premium piece, at 66,000 yen. While supplies last, fans purchasing the collaboration items will get them placed inside an Evangelion/Hard Rock shopping bag. The lineup goes on sale November 3, with the exception of the pin which is scheduled to be available sometime in “early November.” Related: Hard Rock Cafe Japan location list Source: PR Times via Nijimen Images: PR Times ● Want to hear about SoraNews24’s latest articles as soon as they’re published? title: Hello Kitty cuts ties with hit Japanese spy drama Vivant over torture scenes
summary: Goodbye Kitty. Vivant has emerged as a major hit on Japanese TV to a degree that only seems to come along every decade or so. It stars Masato Sakai, who also starred in Japan’s last gigantic TV hit Hanzawa Naoki, by the same director, with Sakai this time playing a businessman who gets embroiled in […]
details: Goodbye Kitty . Vivant has emerged as a major hit on Japanese TV to a degree that only seems to come along every decade or so. It stars Masato Sakai, who also starred in Japan’s last gigantic TV hit Hanzawa Naoki , by the same director, with Sakai this time playing a businessman who gets embroiled in international intrigue. The program has become so popular that it is frequently involved in tie-ups with other brands eager to ride the Vivant wave. And there is perhaps no company that loves collaborating more than Sanrio, which has teamed up with just about everything from Sesame Street and Clinique to Pringles and Godzilla . Earlier this year, various goods such as plush toys and T-shirts featured six of Sanrio’s most popular characters dressed as the characters from Vivant . Nogitty was a mash-up of Hello Kitty and Sakai’s character Yusuke Nogi, while Hangyodon took on the role of Mamoru Nozaki, played by Hiroshi Abe in the show. There were also My Melody, Pompompurin, Cinnamoroll, and Kuromi as Kaoru Yuzuki, Drum, Nokoru, and Kurosu respectively. ＼明日まで／ G階段下ワゴンで開催中の VIVANT POP-UP SHOPは7/16の18時まで！ グッズをゲットして、 7/26(日)から始まるTBS系日曜劇場『 #VIVANT 』第2シーズンを観よう ！ #サンリオキャラクターズ #東京キャラクターストリート #キャラスト pic.twitter.com/lOJhVVmhI7 — 【公式】東京キャラクターストリート (@characterstreet) July 15, 2026 I’m using past tense there because as of 29 October, all of the Sanrio Vivant items have been taken off the market . On October 28, Sanrio’s Chinese arm, Sanrio Shanghai International Trading, announced, through its social media account, the cancellation of Sanrio’s collaboration with Vivant and that all future activities related to it would be cancelled as well. Sanrio Japan also posted a statement on October 29 announcing the cancelation of the collaboration, apologizing for any discomfort it may have caused and that the themes of the show were inconsistent with Sanrio’s corporate philosophy of “One world, connecting smiles.” A few days earlier, Chinese state-run media had published a piece on Vivant , accusing it of slandering China and “exaggerating the China threat theory,” referring to the idea that China’s rapid growth poses a fundamental threat to global peace and stability. This all stems from scenes in Vivant that show a fictional organization affiliated with China brutally torturing members of the fictional Japanese covert group Beppan, hacking all of the fingers off one member’s hand. Problematic Japanese-Chinese relations aside, reading that last sentence would make one wonder what Hello Kitty was doing with this show in the first place. Granted, Sanrio has been known to dabble in dark franchises in the past, but close association with torture and mutilation might not be good optics for the maker of Dokidoki Yummychums. It’s an opinion shared by many in online comments as well. “It was an odd combination to begin with.” “I always thought Sanrio avoided collaborating with themes involving things like the military or war. How did Vivant get the green light?” “I guess this was a miscalculation on Sanrio’s part. Maybe they didn’t anticipate this kind of explicit and controversial content from Vivant.” “It was cancelled before I could buy anything! I was planning to get something next month, too.” “This is hardly surprising. I’m guessing Masato Sakai won’t be finding much work in China either.” “Sanrio needs to put more thought into who they team up with.“ As for Vivant ’s response to the criticism from China, the network that airs it, TBS, released a statement saying they will seriously consider questions that the show “harbors hostility towards certain countries” and features excessive violence. While they maintain that the torture scenes were necessary to the show’s story, they also say they will continue to carefully consider whether certain depictions will cause discomfort or excessive fear among viewers. We’ll see how that goes, but hopefully Hello Kitty learned her lesson and will stick with more family-friendly fare like It … I’m guessing they didn’t read the book. title: Real-world Legend of Zelda treasures, Heart Container lights and Ruppe pouches, coming soon [Pics]
summary: Whether you’re restoring your energy at home or out adventuring in the world, these Hyrulian artifacts will be ready to help. Nintendo fans already have November 5 circled on their calendars, since that’s when the long-awaited remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time goes on sale for the Switch 2. That’s not the […]
details: Whether you’re restoring your energy at home or out adventuring in the world, these Hyrulian artifacts will be ready to help . Nintendo fans already have November 5 circled on their calendars, since that’s when the long-awaited remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time goes on sale for the Switch 2. That’s not the only cool Zelda -related release coming up in November though, with Japanese fashion and interior company Takarajimasha , whose name means “treasure island company,” releasing two creations based on treasure from Nintendo’s fantasy franchise . The first item is a replica of the coveted Heart Container , which has been extending the hero Link’s maximum life bar since the very start of the series. Takarajimasha’s version is modeled on the version seen in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom with its arabesque gold framing. While this real-world won’t instantly increase your longevity or resilience, it can provide illumination, as it’s actually a 9-centimeter (3.5-inch) tall lamp that produces a warm red glow when switched on . The designers know that you will want to hold this in your hands, so the lamp can be detached from the base. ▼ Though you’ll have to hum Zelda’s traditional four-note “treasure found” fanfare yourself. Because of their value and rarity, Heart Containers are something that players search high and low for in exploring the games’ realms, but Takarajimasha also wants to salute the most common of Zelda treasures, the humble Rupee . The green Ruppe, the smallest-denomination of Hyrulian currency, is something you’ll collect hundreds of, if not thousands, during a playthrough of one of the Zelda games, and yet, it’s still sure to bring a smile to you, or any fellow fans, when one shows up in our world as a zippered silicone pouch . The designers bill is as a komono ire , a Japanese term whose closest English equivalent would be “accessory pouch,” but really refers to a pouch for storing any small items, such as earbuds, cosmetics, or even bite-sized snacks. There’s a strap in case you want to use it as a bag charm, and you’ll also find The Legend of Zelda , written in Japanese, on the Rupee’s underside . A quirk of the Japanese publishing industry is that fashion and lifestyle magazines sometimes come with some sort of fashion/lifestyle item bundled with them. Sometimes these are so popular that they overshadow the edition of the periodical, so, noticing this, companies like Takarajimasha that specialize in such bundled items sometimes flip the script and make the items the primary product and toss in a mini magazine as a supplementary freebie. Both the Heart Container Interior Light and the Rupee Silicone Pouch are being offered in this format, branded as “Books” and sold together with an eight-page booklet of undisclosed but presumably Zelda -related nature . The Heart Container light is priced at 3,839 yen (US$24) and the Rupee pouch at 2,992 yen. They both go on sale November 2 and can be ordered, here and here , through the Takarajimasha online shop as well as through select branches of convenience store chain Lawson. summary: Combining palanquins and muscle suits to make historic sites accessible for all. details: Combining palanquins and muscle suits to make historic sites accessible for all. Along the eastern shores of Lake Biwa, Japan’s largest freshwater lake, in Shiga is the city of Hikone , home to one of only twelve castles in Japan with its original main keep still standing. However, reaching the top is not a casual stroll, being guarded by 140 steep, irregular stone steps explicitly designed to exhaust invading samurai, and now those same steps present a modern dilemma. Being a National Special Historic Site , and a possible candidate for UNESCO World Cultural Heritage status in 2028, how can the site be made more accessible for visitors who use wheelchairs or have mobility impairments, especially when pouring concrete ramps over 17th-century masonry isn’t exactly an option that would be enthusiastically received? On October 19, Hikone City staff and volunteers conducted a trial, where they took turns acting as carriers, carrying wheelchair users up to the main enclosure ( honmaru ) using a traditional wooden mountain palanquin ( yamakago ). The trek covered a 285-meter (935-foot) round-trip with a 50-meter (165-foot) vertical rise and an average 18-percent incline, which is not an easy feat for two people to do. So, to lighten the load for the team of six carriers, trial participants strapped on state-of-the-art, non-motorized wearable assist suits , with two wearing the Muscle Suit Soft-Power Easy-Lift and four equipping the Mediaid Firm Guard Waist EX Hard . ▼Muscle Suit Soft-Power Easy-Lift ▼Mediaid Firm Guard Waist EX Hard The reaction from the carriers was enthusiastic , receiving comments like: “Because I injured my lower back in the past, wearing it gave me a real sense of security.” “It is attached at the base of the knees, but when standing upright it is loose, so it does not get in the way of going up and down the stairs.” “The moment I took it off, I realized just how much it had been helping me.” Standing up while balancing a palanquin on your shoulders normally feels like tipping backward, causing some difficulty in maintaining balance, but the back-and-leg support makes rising smooth and stable. Beyond opening up easier physical access to a historic tourist site, the trial offered a glimpse into an exciting future for Japanese tourism , with accompanying curators explaining the history and scenery of the location, creating an opportunity for visitors to get a taste of what it would be like to travel around the mountain like nobility in the time of the samurai. Similarly, it could also open up another bucket-list item for many travelers along with sitting on the back of a human-powered rickshaw , being chauffeured around Japan’s historical districts. If wearable assist suits can help bridge the gap between 17th-century architecture and 21st-century accessibility, it opens up countless possibilities for historic castles, mountain temples, and heritage sites all across Japan. details: Kiki’s Delivery Service scene-stealer is adorably transfixed by Donguri Kyowakoku’s latest homeware offering . Any branch of Ghibli specialty shop chain Donguri Kyowakoku will be filled with amazing merch from the anime studio’s films, but a few locations are extra-special thanks to their inclusion of items from the Donguri Closet sub-brand. As the name alludes to, Donguri Closet’s focus is on fashion and home décor. The designs have an elegant coziness to them, making them the sort of things that, without being flashy, will catch the eyes of fans as soon as they step into the room…and, in this case, catch the eyes of Kiki’s Delivery Service’s Jiji too. So what’s got Kiki’s black cat companion so captivated? A recreation of an oil lamp seen in the home of Osono, the kindly baker who Kiki and Jiji rent a room from after arriving in the city where the anime’s story takes place . Though made of resin and ABS for extra sturdiness, the intricate details and delicate coloring give it a look evocative of antique porcelain. The clear top section of the lamp is made of glass, but since the logistics hassles and safety risks of burning an actual oil lamp can be a hassle to deal with, this is an electric light. The designers have cleverly hid the main power switch on the underside of the base, though, to better sell the illusion of old-timey-ness, and the light can be turned on or off with a tap of your finger thanks to a touch sensor embedded in the lamp . Officially called the Kiki’s Delivery Service Mini Lamp-Mitsumeru Jiji (“Transfixed Jiji”), the piece is 12.8 centimeters (5 inches) tall and 11.2 centimeters wide, putting it right in that sweet spot where it’s neither too small to be noticed nor too big to be in the way. Priced at 13,200 yen (US$83), it’ll be available at select Donguri Kyowakoku stores in Tokyo (Ikebukuro, Skytree Town Solamachi), Nagoya (Takashimaya Gate Tower Mall), Osaka (Lucua Osaka), Fukuoka (Canal City Hakata), and Sapporo (Sapporo Parco), as well as through the Donguri Kyowakoku online store here starting October 31. title: De los creadores de Date A Live: El anime King's Proposal se estrenará en 2027
summary: El anime King's Proposal, de los creadores de Date A Live, confirmó su estreno para 2027 y la voz de Rie Takahashi.
details: Anime De los creadores de Date A Live: El anime King's Proposal se estrenará en 2027 La adaptación de las novelas ligeras producidas por Aniplex llegará a las pantallas en 2027. Kudasai hace 2 horas 3 Comentarios ADS Los creadores de una de las comedias románticas y de ciencia ficción más queridas de la última década están listos para conquistar la pantalla chica con una propuesta completamente nueva. La compañía Aniplex presentó formalmente los primeros detalles oficiales para la adaptación al anime de King's Proposal ( Ousama no Propose ), confirmando que la serie se estrenará en algún punto de 2027 y revelando a la reconocida actriz de voz que liderará el reparto principal. Durante una presentación especial, la distribuidora compartió una primera imagen promocional del proyecto junto con la confirmación de que la talentosa Rie Takahashi prestará su voz a la protagonista, Saika Kuozaki. La historia nos presenta a Saika como la maga más poderosa del mundo, la única capaz de detener a las misteriosas entidades que intentan destruir el planeta cada 300 horas. Sin embargo, tras caer gravemente herida en combate, decide heredar sus poderes y su propio cuerpo a un estudiante de preparatoria común llamado Mushiki Kuga. Tener las habilidades de la hechicera suprema no significa saber dominarlas, por lo que el joven Mushiki se verá obligado a ingresar a una academia de magia tomando la apariencia física de Saika. Su misión no solo será aprender a controlar este poder inconmensurable para salvar a la humanidad, sino también mantener su verdadera identidad masculina oculta ante todo el mundo. Este esperado anime recupera el proyecto que había sido anunciado por primera vez durante una transmisión en vivo en octubre de 2025, comenzando a tomar forma rumbo a su lanzamiento definitivo en 2027. Sobre King's Proposal King's Proposal es una saga de novelas ligeras de fantasía y comedia escrita por Koushi Tachibana e ilustrada por Tsunako , la misma dupla creativa detrás del fenómeno internacional Date A Live . La obra impresa comenzó su publicación en octubre de 2021 bajo el sello de la editorial Kadokawa, habiendo lanzado su octavo volumen en agosto de 2025 y con su noveno tomo programado para llegar a las librerías este 18 de diciembre. La franquicia contó además con una adaptación al manga ilustrada por Nemo Kurio en el portal Gangan Online de Square Enix, la cual concluyó en marzo de 2025 con un total de seis volúmenes recopilatorios. ¿Qué te parece la premisa de King's Proposal y la elección de Rie Takahashi para el papel principal? Manga Fallece Tetsuya Chiba, leyenda del manga y creador de Ashita no Joe

title: Fallece Tetsuya Chiba, leyenda del manga y creador de Ashita no Joe
summary: El mangaka Tetsuya Chiba, creador de Ashita no Joe y pionero de la industria, falleció en Tokio a los 87 años.
details: Manga Fallece Tetsuya Chiba, leyenda del manga y creador de Ashita no Joe El legendario dibujante padecía un síndrome mielodisplásico y se despidió a los 87 años. Aiko hace 6 segundos 0 Comentarios ADS Hay noticias que golpean directo en el corazón de la historia de la cultura pop japonesa. El legendario dibujante y autor de manga Tetsuya Chiba , reconocido en todo el planeta por dar vida al inolvidable manga deportivo Ashita no Joe , falleció el pasado 22 de octubre a los 87 años en un hospital de Tokio tras enfrentar complicaciones derivadas de un síndrome mielodisplásico, un tipo de cáncer que afecta las células sanguíneas en la médula ósea. El maestro Chiba se había visto obligado a pausar la publicación de su obra autobiográfica Hinemosu Notari Nikki en la revista Big Comic el pasado 25 de septiembre debido al deterioro de su estado de salud. En los últimos años, el dibujante había batallado con diversos problemas médicos, incluyendo una cirugía cardíaca en 2022 para colocarle un stent, procedimientos oculares y tratamientos contra un tumor en la garganta. A pesar de estas dificultades, se mantuvo activo y conectado con su público hasta donde sus fuerzas se lo permitieron. A lo largo de su impresionante trayectoria, Chiba acumuló los mayores honores que un creador puede recibir en el país nipón. En 2022 fue nominado a la Academia de Arte de Japón junto a Yoshiharu Tsuge, convirtiéndose en uno de los primeros creadores de manga en recibir esta distinción. De igual forma, ocupó la presidencia de la Asociación de Caricaturistas de Japón y en 2024 hizo historia al ser galardonado con la Orden de la Cultura, siendo el primer autor de manga en la historia en recibir semejante condecoración de parte del gobierno japonés. Ashita no Joe es una de las obras más trascendentales e influyentes en la historia del manga y la animación japonesa. Escrita por Ikki Kajiwara e ilustrada por Tetsuya Chiba , la historia se serializó entre 1968 y 1973, convirtiéndose en un verdadero fenómeno social que trascendió las páginas impresas para marcar a toda una generación. El argumento sigue el duro camino de Joe Yabuki, un joven huérfano y rebelde de los barrios bajos de Tokio que encuentra en el boxeo una razón de vivir y luchar. El legado de la obra inspiró dos icónicas adaptaciones animadas para televisión en 1970 y 1980, así como dos largometrajes cinematográficos. Años más tarde, el espíritu de la serie fue reimaginado en un entorno futurista con la aclamada producción Megalobox en 2018 y su secuela Megalobox 2: Nomad en 2021. La obra de Chiba sentó las bases del género deportivo moderno y su estilo de dibujo sigue siendo un pilar fundamental sobre el cual se construyó la industria actual. ¿Tuviste la oportunidad de leer Ashita no Joe o conocer su legado a través de Megalobox? title: Tras 22 años de historia, el anime de Bleach llega a su final definitivo
summary: El anime de Bleach emitió su episodio final de Thousand-Year Blood War, concluyendo 22 años de historia.
details: Anime Tras 22 años de historia, el anime de Bleach llega a su final definitivo El episodio 50 de Thousand-Year Blood War cierra la historia de Ichigo Kurosaki. Mirukaru hace 1 hora 4 Comentarios ADS Si creciste viendo a los Shinigami enfrentarse a los Hollows en la televisión o leyendo cada capítulo semana a semana, prepara los pañuelos porque una era dorada ha llegado a su fin. La adaptación animada de Bleach concluyó oficialmente su transmisión tras 22 años de historia con la emisión del episodio número 50 de Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War - The Calamity , marcando el cierre definitivo de las aventuras de Ichigo Kurosaki en la pantalla chica. El episodio final, titulado significativamente "DEATH & STRAWBERRY", nos traslada diez años después de los acontecimientos de la gran guerra por la protección del Rey Espiritual. La trama muestra cómo los sobrevivientes de aquella feroz batalla avanzan hacia sus respectivos futuros, cerrando el ciclo con la aparición de Kazui Kurosaki e Ichika Abarai, los jóvenes integrantes que representan a la nueva generación de esta inolvidable franquicia. Al término de la emisión, el equipo de producción regaló a la audiencia un vídeo especial de cierre acompañado por el emblemático tema musical "Number One". Este metraje de créditos exhibe bocetos clave de la animación y concluye con una huella pisando la palabra "desesperación" grabada en una tierra baldía, revelando la palabra "BRAVE" junto al mensaje "THE STORIES OF BRAVE". Sumado a esto, se publicó el recopilatorio THE STORIES VISUAL MOVIE , un repaso que reúne las quince facetas visuales de Ichigo Kurosaki desde sus inicios como Shinigami sustituto hasta su versión adulta una década después del conflicto. Para quienes deseen conservar este hito histórico en su colección, el paquete Blu-ray y DVD BOX IV, que abarca desde el episodio 41 hasta el 50, se pondrá a la venta el próximo 24 de marzo de 2027 junto a la tercera banda sonora oficial. Ambos lanzamientos incluirán ilustraciones inéditas realizadas por el diseñador de personajes Masashi Kudo. Bleach es una de las franquicias más icónicas del shonen contemporáneo, nacida de la pluma y el dibujo del autor Tite Kubo . El manga original comenzó su publicación en la revista Weekly Shonen Jump en 2001 y concluyó en 2016, superando la impresionante cifra de 130 millones de copias en circulación a nivel global. Su primera adaptación al anime arrancó en 2004, convirtiéndose rápidamente en un referente indiscutible de la cultura pop japonesa junto a otros gigantes de su época. Tras años de espera, el arco final del manga inició su adaptación animada en 2022 bajo el título Thousand-Year Blood War , dividida en cuatro partes para adaptar con la máxima fidelidad y calidad visual el desenlace de la obra. Con la transmisión de su cuarta parte concluyendo este 26 de octubre, la saga de Tite Kubo se despide por todo lo alto dejando un legado imborrable en varias generaciones de espectadores. ¿Qué te pareció el final de Bleach y qué emoción te deja decir adiós a Ichigo después de tantos años? title: El anime secuela de BanG Dream! Ave Mujica confirma su fecha de estreno para 2027
summary: La secuela al anime de BanG Dream! It's MyGO!!!!! y Ave Mujica confirmó su fecha de estreno oficial para el 8 de enero de 2027.
details: Anime El anime secuela de BanG Dream! Ave Mujica confirma su fecha de estreno para 2027 La secuela que reunirá a MyGO!!!!! y Ave Mujica se estrenará en televisión el 8 de enero de 2027. Kudasai hace 1 hora 0 Comentarios ADS El drama, los malentendidos y la música estridente entre chicas de preparatoria están lejos de terminar, y las bandas más intensas de la franquicia ya tienen todo listo para su próximo gran asalto. El equipo detrás de BanG Dream! It's MyGO!!!!! // Ave Mujica presentó un nuevo avance en vídeo que confirmó de manera oficial que la esperada secuela en formato de serie de televisión se estrenará el 8 de enero de 2027 . Este nuevo proyecto promete darle continuidad directa a la tormentosa relación entre las integrantes de MyGO!!!!! y Ave Mujica, dos agrupaciones que han revolucionado por completo el tono de la franquicia en sus entregas más recientes. El anuncio vino acompañado por un segundo vídeo promocional que dejó ver los primeros destellos de la tensión narrativa que marcará esta nueva etapa televisiva, generando una enorme expectativa entre los seguidores que han seguido de cerca cada giro en la historia de estas jóvenes músicas. La franquicia ha tenido un ritmo de lanzamientos impresionante en la pantalla grande y en televisión durante los últimos años. La primera entrega centrada en Ave Mujica llegó a las pantallas japonesas el 2 de enero de 2025, seguida por el proyecto cinematográfico titulado BanG Dream! Ave Mujica prima aurora , el cual celebró su estreno en cines el pasado 16 de octubre. De igual forma, la serie original de MyGO!!!!! que se emitió en junio de 2023 contó con dos películas recopilatorias lanzadas a finales de 2024: Haru no Hidamari, Mayoi Neko en septiembre y Utau, Bokura ni Nareru Uta en noviembre. Sobre BanG Dream! BanG Dream! es un exitoso proyecto multimedia de música y chicas de preparatoria lanzado por la compañía Bushiroad en enero de 2015. La franquicia combina grupos musicales de la vida real formados por actrices de voz con proyectos de animación, videojuegos para dispositivos móviles, mangas y conciertos presenciales de gran escala a nivel internacional. La historia televisiva arrancó oficialmente en enero de 2017 con su primera temporada de trece episodios, dando paso años más tarde a una tercera temporada en enero de 2020. A lo largo de su trayectoria, la saga ha expandido su universo con largometrajes como FILM LIVE y su secuela, el proyecto en dos partes Episode of Roselia , además de múltiples producciones derivadas para internet. ¿Estás listo para reencontrarte con el drama de MyGO!!!!! y la oscuridad de Ave Mujica en 2027? title: Las villanas toman el control: El anime Dual Shadow Precure se estrenara en 2027
summary: Toei Animation anunció el anime derivado Dual Shadow Precure Villain Heroines con historia y personajes originales para 2027.
details: Anime Las villanas toman el control: El anime Dual Shadow Precure se estrenara en 2027 Toei Animation confirma una historia con personajes originales enfocada en villanas para 2027. Ryo hace 33 minutos 0 Comentarios ADS Las chicas mágicas más emblemáticas de la industria están listas para dar un giro inesperado a su fórmula tradicional. La compañía Toei Animation confirmó la producción de una nueva serie derivada para la franquicia de Magical Girls titulada Dual Shadow Precure Villain Heroines , un proyecto televisivo programado para llegar a las pantallas en 2027 que pondrá los reflectores sobre un ángulo completamente diferente dentro de este colorido universo. A diferencia de la gran mayoría de entregas secundarias dentro de la saga, esta producción apostará por una narrativa totalmente inédita acompañada por personajes originales creados desde cero. El avance conceptual liberado por la productora comienza mostrando un brillante campo repleto de flores que cambia de tono de forma drástica, presentando la frase "De todas formas no somos Precure" mientras una sola flor permanece bajo un foco de luz con miradas inquietantes observando desde el fondo. La inclusión del término "Villain" en el título oficial no es ninguna casualidad. La franquicia cuenta con una rica tradición donde las enemigas terminan convirtiéndose en heroínas con el paso de la trama, un concepto que se consolidó en 2009 con la transformación de Higashi Setsuna, conocida originalmente como Eas en Fresh Precure! , para asumir la identidad de Cure Passion. En esta ocasión, la historia promete explorar a fondo esa delgada línea entre el bien y el mal, cuestionando qué significa ser una verdadera heroína desde la perspectiva de quienes habitan en las sombras. Precure ( Pretty Cure ) es una de las franquicias de chicas mágicas más longevas y exitosas producidas por el estudio Toei Animation desde su debut en 2004. A lo largo de más de dos décadas, la saga se ha caracterizado por renovar sus conceptos, temáticas y elenco de protagonistas año tras año, convirtiéndose en un referente indispensable de la animación japonesa contemporánea. Actualmente, la franquicia mantiene en emisión su entrega número 23 titulada Star Detective Precure! , la cual se estrenó el 1 de febrero y contó con su propia película cinematográfica en septiembre. Además, la saga ha explorado proyectos conmemorativos como la serie de 2023 Power of Hope: Precure Full Bloom , que sirvió como secuela con las protagonistas en edad adulta, así como Maho Tsukai Precure!!: MIRAI DAYS estrenada en 2025. Con este nuevo paso hacia historias con tintes más oscuros, la marca demuestra que aún tiene bastantes sorpresas reservadas para sus seguidores. ¿Qué te parece que las villanas tomen el protagonismo en este nuevo anime de la saga? Manga Fallece Tetsuya Chiba, leyenda del manga y creador de Ashita no Joe

title: One Piece Chapter 1197: Release date & major spoilers
summary: Discover when One Piece Chapter 1197 will be released as all the major spoilers are revealed.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 TV & Movies Anime One Piece Chapter 1197: Release date & major spoilers by Anamika Das Published: Oct 28, 2026, 15:26 Save for later Save for later Fuji Television Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News One Piece Chapter 1197 has Sanji overcoming his self-hatred and overpowering his opponent, so here’s when it releases and what to expect. The Straw Hats’ chef is one of the most well-written characters in the series. Throughout the story, we see Sanji risking his life again and again to defeat his foes. His self-sacrificing nature is finally explained in the Whole Cake Island Arc, where we learn of the abuse he endured in his childhood. Article continues after ad Sanji’s tendency to get intentionally hurt is explored again in Chapter 1196 , when he remembers his time in the Kamabokko Kingdom. At that time, Ivankov advised him to love himself before anything else if he really wanted to protect the people he cared about. In One Piece Chapter 1197, Sanji embraces his past hurt and becomes the warrior Luffy needs him to be. This also signals that the Holy Knights’ time on Elbaf is about to be over. Article continues after ad Article continues after ad One Piece Chapter 1197 release date and time One Piece Chapter 1197 will be released on Sunday, November 1, 2026, at 7am PT . You can read the latest chapter for free on Manga Plus and find out its global release time zones below: 11am Eastern Time 4pm British Time 5pm European Time 8:30pm Indian Time 11pm Philippine Time One Piece Chapter 1197 major spoilers Shueisha Titled ‘Love is Defense,’ One Piece Chapter 1197 gives a nod to Ivankov’s advice to Sanji about self-love. The chapter focuses entirely on his fight against Killingham. The chapter starts with Sanji contemplating how his body has carried him through many fights and suffered so much. He realizes that protecting it should be his priority. Flashback panels show key figures in Sanji’s life, including Judge, Zeff, and the opponents he faced. Related One Piece Chapter 1196: Release date & major spoilers One Piece Chapter 1195: Release date & major spoilers One Piece Chapter 1193: Release date & major spoilers Article continues after ad Sanji also realizes that his hatred for his own body came from his childhood. He’s always hated his siblings’ bodies and thought he’d rather die than have a body like theirs. This has led him to deliberately risk his own body over the years. Article continues after ad Sanji understands that ordinary Armament Haki won’t be enough to defeat Killingham. He needs a stronger defense to counter the immortal man. He unleashes a barrage of kicks, irritating Killingham so much that the Holy Knight coats himself with black armor through Omen that can Article continues after ad only be broken with the Conqueror’s Haki. Sanji conjures new flames around his leg that look similar to Ifrit Jambe, but the flames’ aura is more fluid. When he blocks Killingham’s attack with it, the tip of Longinus shatters, and Sanji is thrown away by the impact. As Sanji inspects the flames, he finds that his Armament Haki has reached a new level. He no longer feels pain and can now withstand any attack with ease, as if he’s the one attacking. He may even shatter bullets with them. Article continues after ad He stands up, ready to face Killingham. He thinks about how Zoro should be Luffy’s sword, whereas he’d act as his captain’s shield. Black lightning appears around him, indicating that Sanji has finally unlocked his Conqueror’s Haki. Article continues after ad One Piece Chapter 1197 ends with Sanji unleashing a new attack with his flames and Conqueror’s Haki. It shatters the shaft of Longinus and Killingham’s helmet. The last panel shows the Holy Knight spitting blood. Article continues after ad There’ll be no break next week, meaning One Piece will continue with its usual release schedule. Until the next chapter drops, check out our ranking of the best One Piece villains . title: Japanese government still lists refusing to pay for dates as a form of domestic violence
summary: Once again, there’s a lot of nuance that’s lost in the attempt to be succinct. As you can probably guess from its name, the Japanese government’s Gender Equality Bureau isn’t a fan of imbalance in interpersonal relationships. What is surprising to many people, though, is the bureau’s assertion that “not paying for any dating expenses” […]
details: Once again, there’s a lot of nuance that’s lost in the attempt to be succinct . As you can probably guess from its name, the Japanese government’s Gender Equality Bureau isn’t a fan of imbalance in interpersonal relationships. What is surprising to many people, though, is the bureau’s assertion that “not paying for any dating expenses” is committing an act of domestic violence . On its website, the bureau lists four categories of “dating domestic violence.” Examples of “physical violence” are pretty obvious – striking, pulling hair, throwing objects, that sort of thing. “Sexual violence,” the bureau says, includes coerced sex, refusal to use contraception, and nonconsensual naked photography or video recording. “Psychological violence” is described as making insulting or disrespectful remarks, forbidding a romantic partner from seeing their friends, or monitoring their email communications. It’s bureau discussion of “economic violence,” though, that’s been raising some eyebrows online in Japan this week. While one could argue that this is using the word “violence” in its broadest possible sense, most of the examples are things that would be considered wrong under basic common sense/decency, such as not paying back money borrowed from a romantic partner, taking money from their bank account without permission, and forbidding them to work outside the home or forcing them to quit their job. But then there’s this example of economic violence: “Not paying for any dating expenses.” Japan may not have a reputation for being the most chivalrous society, and going Dutch, or warikan , as it’s called in Japanese, is more common in casual dating here than it is in some other countries. That said, it’s not at all unusual for guys to pay for everything on a date with a girl, and the government of Japan saying that this is a form of domestic violence has been provoking a lot of responses online to a recent Twitter post pointing out the bureau’s stance. “Yeah, it’s practically theft, so it’s obviously a form of domestic abuse.” “Wait, I’ve never made a girl pay on a date, so does that mean that I’ve been subjected to economic violence in the eyes of the government?” “There are a lot of guys who are the victim of this kind of domestic abuse.” “Does this make guys who habitually treat the girl on dates masochists for actively encouraging dating domestic violence?” “Let’s all make sure to properly split the bill, because the government has said that anything other than that is considered economic violence, OK?” “That’ll show all those gold-digger girls who hang out in Tokyo’s Minato Ward.” “This is wonderful for men. I think all us guys are thinking ‘Hey, can’t you pitch in a little?’ but we can’t say it to the girl because we’re trying to look cool.” “Coerced treating is a crime.” “I think they mean it’s wrong for both guys and girls to refuse to pay for dating expenses.” There’s probably at least a little wry humor behind some of those comments, but the last two are the ones that really get to the heart of the matter. As clarified by a spokesperson for the Gender Equality Bureau when this example of economic violence also became a topic of online discussion a few years ago , the bureau recognizes that “Both men and women can be victims of this kind of violence” and that “If both sides are OK with [one person not paying], it’s not domestic violence.” It’s when one person attempts to force their partner to shoulder all of the dating costs against their will that it crosses the line into unacceptable behavior, or when someone demands to be reimbursed for past dating expenses that, at the time, they offered to pay for. ▼ Just like going to a butcher shop on a date is fine if that’s what both you and your sweetheart are into, so too is it OK if you’re in agreement that you’ll be treating her to a half-kilo of ground beef. In other words, the bureau’s guidelines are more about discouraging someone from unilaterally declaring “We’re going out, and you’re going to pay for me” or becoming verbally abusive if asked to chip in, not shaming someone for consistently accepting offers to be treated . But while we’re on the subject of “other words,” as mentioned above, this is not the first time the vague language used on the bureau’s website regarding who pays on a date has caused confusion, and the list of examples being followed by the declaration that “All of these are violence” leaves the door open to misinterpretation that context and a couple’s specific circumstances are irrelevant. The statement has remained on the site in its current form since 2018, so maybe it’s time for an update that puts a finer point on things. title: Starbucks Japan releases “Let’s Par-TEA!” Frappuccino and drinks for the holiday season
summary: Each beverage has its own unique character so you can choose which one you’d like to party with. With the holiday season fast approaching, Starbucks is bringing the party spirit to its stores in Japan with a trio of new drinks based around the theme of “Let’s par-TEA!” As the name suggests, the three new holiday […]
details: Each beverage has its own unique character so you can choose which one you’d like to party with. With the holiday season fast approaching, Starbucks is bringing the party spirit to its stores in Japan with a trio of new drinks based around the theme of “ Let’s par-TEA! ” As the name suggests, the three new holiday drinks shine a spotlight on tea, with strawberry , royal milk tea and Earl Grey chocolate featuring in the beverages. The three stars of this tea party each have their own distinct character, so you can choose the one that best suits your mood. Those wanting an elegant pick-me-up can opt for the Joyful Medley Strawberry Creamy Tea Latte , which combines robust black tea with the smooth sweetness of oolong tea and the floral fragrance of jasmine tea, finished with a subtle hint of apricot. ▼ Joyful Medley Strawberry Creamy Tea Latte (Tall size only, 638 yen [US$4.03] for takeout; 650 yen for dine-in) The blended tea base is joined by sweetened fresh cream and a topping of strawberry-flavoured mousse and freeze-dried strawberries. The rich aroma of the chain’s famous Joyful Medley blend, which is reminiscent of apricot jam, is layered with creamy sweetness, while the finish remains refreshing, allowing you to enjoy a variety of tastes and aromas throughout the beverage. ▼ Earl Grey Chocolate Frappuccino (Tall size only, 678 yen takeout; 690 yen dine-in) Those wanting a little more playfulness can reward themselves with this tea-and-chocolate Frappuccino, which combines aromatic Earl Grey with rich chocolate sauce and crunchy chocolate chips. It has a mellow, layered flavour, with the gentle fragrance of bergamot and the taste of black tea spreading through the palate with every sip, while the chocolate chips add crunchy textural contrast, capturing the playful spirit of the holiday season. ▼ Royal Milk Tea (609 yen takeout; 620 yen dine-in) Finally, we have a rich, blended milk tea that combines milk with an original blend of three teas: Darjeeling , Assam and Ceylon . The full-bodied flavour of the tea harmonises with the mellow creaminess of the milk, creating a rich and rewarding taste that tea lovers will fall in love with. As an extra special holiday treat, Starbucks is also adding a cookie option, so you can add more flavour and a dash of cuteness to any iced beverage that’s topped with whipped cream or mousse foam. ▼ Be a Santa Cookie Topping (69 yen takeout; 70 yen dine-in) The “Be a Santa Cookie Topping” has a buttery aroma and crisp yet crumbly shortbread texture. The three designs – a present, a Christmas tree and a Santa hat – are provided at random so, like a Christmas present, you won’t know what you’re getting until it’s given to you by the barista. While the cookie topping will be available while stocks last from 2-19 November, the drinks will be on the menu for a limited (but unspecified) time from 2 November. title: Shinkansen online ticketing service reports customer data leak
summary: Online reservation system handles tickets for Shinkansen’s “Golden Route” and Kyushu. If you’re planning to take a ride on the Shinkansen, the Smart EX online ticketing service is a handy utility. Managed by Shinkansen operator Central Japan Railway Company/JR Central, Smart EX lets you book seats on bullet trains running in eastern and western Japan, […]
details: Online reservation system handles tickets for Shinkansen’s “Golden Route” and Kyushu . If you’re planning to take a ride on the Shinkansen , the Smart EX online ticketing service is a handy utility. Managed by Shinkansen operator Central Japan Railway Company/JR Central , Smart EX lets you book seats on bullet trains running in eastern and western Japan, as well as the southwestern island of Kyushu. A wide selection of credit cards can be used for payment, and the Smart EX mobile app can provide you with a QR code so that you don’t have to fuss around with a paper ticket. Unfortunately, it’s not just travelers that have found Smart EX alluring, but hackers too, as JR Central has announced a data breach has resulted in personal information of roughly 170,000 Smart EX users being leaked . The incident stems from another security breach earlier this month at Yumirulink, a digital marketing and email forwarding service involved in the routing of some Smart EX messages. Thankfully, the Smart EX user data that was stolen is of a limited scope. According to JR Central’s statement, hackers were able to obtain the users’ names, email addresses, member IDs/screen names, and membership types . Date of birth, home addresses, phone numbers, and credit card numbers and expiration dates were not leaked, the company says. In addition, JR Central says that only the renderings of users’ names in Japanese katakana phonetic characters were leaked, and other forms were not compromised. However, it’s somewhat unclear if this assertion applies only to non-katakana Japanese text (i.e. kanji-character) versions of user names, or if it also is meant to cover names written in the Latin alphabet, since as of this writing the Smart EX website only has a statement regarding the data leak on its Japanese-language page, with no mention of it on the service’s English site. JR Central’s statement also says that the data breach was not connected to auto-generated emails such as those that Smart EX sends to confirm bookings or customer-initiated schedule changes, and instead is related to emails sent for things such as sale promotions or altered timetable notifications following the recent Kumamoto earthquake. Collectively, the Smart EX system covers Shinkansen bookings for bullet trains operated by JR Central, JR West, and JR Kyushu , which together stretch from Tokyo through Osaka, Kyoto, and Hiroshima on to Fukuoka and then down to Kagoshima. So if you’ve used the service to book a Shinkansen ticket along that network, it’s probably a good idea to keep an eye on your various other online accounts in the coming days, just in case someone out there has some of your personal data. title: Japan’s super cute tanuki bread skips tricks, promises to be treat for your eyes and taste buds
summary: You can trust this tanuki to be as sweet on the inside as it looks on the outside. In Japanese folklore, tanuki are tricksters. There’s nothing they love more than playing pranks on us unsuspecting humans, and that image of them even extends to Japanese cuisine. “Tanuki soba” and “tanuki udon” are styles of noodles […]
details: You can trust this tanuki to be as sweet on the inside as it looks on the outside . In Japanese folklore, tanuki are tricksters. There’s nothing they love more than playing pranks on us unsuspecting humans, and that image of them even extends to Japanese cuisine. “Tanuki soba” and “tanuki udon” are styles of noodles topped with tempura flakes only, because those crafty racoon dogs have tricked you by already eating the shrimp or veggies that would ordinarily be inside the tempura. But at the same time, tanuki are really, really cute, and thankfully it’s this aspect that Japanese bakery Kimuraya has chosen to focus on for the treats that’ll be coming out of their ovens next month. Called Tanuki-kun (-kun being a form of address in Japanese that’s friendlier and more familiar than -san), these baked goods are the polar opposite from tanuki soba/udon in terms of filling generosity. Inside the bun is a mixture of caramel cream and chocolate chips , promising a richly sweet and satisfying flavor profile with an interesting texture too. On the outside, the tanuki’s facial features are made of chocolate, and the mask-like marking around its eyes, and part of its ears too, are rendered with a chocolate biscuit dough . Kimuraya is a little on the premium-priced side for a Japanese bakery, and the 400-yen (US$2.50) Tanuki-kun is likewise a little more expensive than the average bakery treat, but with something that looks this delicious and adorable, we can make room in our snack budget. The Tanuki-kun goes on sale at Kimuraya bakeries from November 1, but can also be ordered through the Kimuraya online store as of October 28 .
